ראה.def:
H7203. ro

'eh I. רֹאֶה‎ noun [masculine] seer, with article ׳הָר‎ (except 2Sam 15:27); — old name for נָבִיא‎ 1Sam 9:9b, used of Samuel 9:9 a.; 9:11; 9:18; 9:19 and (as archaism) 1Chr 9:22; 26:28; 29:29; of חֲנָנִי‎2Chr 16:7, 10; הֲרוֺאֶה‎ apparently of Zadok 2Sam 15:27, but corrupt (conjecture in We Dr); plural (with preposition) לָרֹאִים‎ Isa 30:10 the seers, as a class.

II. רֹאֶה‎ noun [masculine] prophetic vision בָּר ׳שָׁגוּ‎ Isa 28:7 they reel in (their) vision (|| מְּלִילִיָּת מָּקוּ‎).

ראובן.def:
H7205. Reuben

רְאוּבֵן‎71 proper name, masculine Reuben, Ρουβην[ιν] (be-hold a son! but Gen 29:32 makes = בְּעָנְיִי רָאָה‎ (!); JosAnt. i. 19, 7 and others Ρουβηλος, ᵑ6‎ , ׳ר‎ then perhaps = Arabic , lion, compare Di); —

1 eldest son of Jacob and Leah Gen 29:32; 30:14 11t. Genesis; Exod 1:2; 1Chr 2:1; as head of family or clan Exod 6:14 (twice in verse); Num 1:20; 26:5 (all P), 1Chr 5:1, 3, compare בֶּןרְֿא אֱלִיאָב ׳בְּנֵי‎ Deut 11:6.

2 as name of clan or tribe Judg 5:15-16, Deut 27:13; Josh 18:7 ( +גָּד‎; both D), Deut 33:6 (poem), Ezek 48:6-7, 31; Num 1:5 (P); so ר ׳מַטֵּה‎ 1:21; 13:4; Josh 20:8; 21:7 (all P), 1Chr 6:48; 6:63, ר ׳מַחֲנֵה‎ Num 2:10, 16; 10:18 (all P); ר ׳בְּנֵי‎, as tribe, Numbers 16:l b 32:37 (both J E), 2:10; 7:20; 26:5; Josh 13:23 (twice in verse) (all P), also (+ Gad and often Manasseh) Num 32:1-2, 6, 25 (JE), Josh 4:12 (D), Num 32:29, 31, 33; Josh 22:9 11t. 22 (all P), compare 1Chr 5:18; ׳בֶּןרֿ‎ as tribe Josh 15:6; 18:7 (both P), ר ׳בְנֵיֿ מַטֵּה‎ 13:15 (P).

ראובני.def:
H7206. Reubeni

רְאוּבֵנִי‎ adjective, of a people of foregoing; of individual 1Chr 11:42 a; with article as substantive collective הָראוּבֵנִי‎ Num 26:7; 34:14 (both P), Josh 13:8 (D; +הַגָּדִי‎), 2Kin 10:33 ( +id. +הַמְנַשִּׁי‎), 1Chr 12:38 (van d. H. v.12:37; +הַגָּדִי‎ +מְנַשֶּׁה שֵׁבֶט חֲצִי‎), 26:32 (id.); לָראוּבֵנִי‎ 5:6; 27:16, +וְלַגָּדִי‎ (+ sometimes מ שֵׁבֶט ׳חֲצִי‎) Deut 3:12, 16; 29:7; Josh 1:12; 12:6; 22:1 (all D), 1Chr 5:26, compare Deut 4:43.

רְאִית רְאָיָה, רֳאִי, רְאִי, ראות,‎ see ראה‎.

רְאֵים‎ see ראישׁון רְאֵם‎ see רִאשׁוֺן‎. p. 911, below

H7200. raah

רָאָה‎1315 verb see (Late Hebrew id.; וארא‎ MI4, הראני‎ Deut 1:7, compare ריח‎ spectacle 1:12; Sabean ראי‎ see, expect DHMZMG xxix (1875), 506, 599; Arabic see, so Ethiopic רֵיוָא רֵו, ᵑ7‎ human appearance, features, etc. (compare Hebrew רְָאִי‎ 2)); —

Qal1141 Perfect3masculine singular ׳ר‎ Gen 29:10 +, suffix וְרָֽאֲךָ‎ consecutive Exod 4:14 רָאָהוּ‎ 2Kin 2:12 +; 3 feminine singular רָֽאֲתָה‎ Gen 38:14, suffix רָאָֽתְךָ‎ Job 42:5; 2masculine singular רָאִיתָ‎ Gen 20:10 +, etc.; Imperfect3masculine singular יִרְהֶ‎ 22:8 +, jussive יֵרֵא‎ 41:33 (Baer Gi, Ges§ 75p, hh Köi.561; van d. H. יֵרֶא‎), יִ֫רֶא‎ Exod 5:21 +, וַיַּרְא‎ Gen 18:2 + (1Sam 19:20, read plural ᵐ5‎ Comm., i.e. וַיִּרְאֻ‎ DrSm lxiii), suffix יִרְאַנִי‎ Exod 33:20, וַיִּרְאֵ֑נִי‎ 2Sam 1:7; 3feminine singular תִּרְאֶה‎ Lev 20:17; Job 33:28, jussive תֵּרֵא‎ Micah 7:10; Zech 9:5 (Baer Gi, compare Ges Kö above; van d. H תֵּרֶא‎), וַתֵּ֫רֶא‎ Gen 3:6 +; 1 singular אֶרְאֶה‎ 21:16 +, וָאֵ֫רֶא‎ 31:10 +, etc.; Imperative רְאֵה‎ 27:27 +, etc.; Infinitive absolute רָאֹה‎ Exod 3:7 +, רָאוֺ‎ Gen 26:28; Isa 6:9; construct רְאֹה‎ Gen 48:11, רְאוֺת‎ Exod 10:28 +, רַאֲוָה‎ Ezek 28:17, etc., Participle active רֹאֶה‎ 13:15 +, etc.; passive רְאֻיוֺת‎ (Baer Gi; van d. H. רְאֻיּוֺת‎) : —

1. a. see, subject עֵינַיִם עַיִן,‎, with accusative of person Isa 6:5; 30:20; Jer 42:2 5t. Job, Proverbs; subject person, with accusative Gen 12:12, 15 + רָאָהוּ מִי‎ 1Sam 23:22, read ᵐ5 הֵמְּהֵרָה‎ Th We and others. [not HPS]); רֹאִי‎ 16:13 (participle suffix, compare רֹאִי לַחֵי בְּאֵר‎ 16:14, .p. 91 above) accusative of God 1Sam 32:31 (אֶלמָּֿנִים מָּנִים‎); accusative of person omitted 18:2; 19:1 +; with accusative מְּנֵי‎ 31:2; 1Sam 46:30; 1Sam 48:11; Exod 33:20, opposed to אֶתאֲחֹרָ֑י‎ 33:23; with accusative מְּנֵי‎ specifically of having access to man of rank Gen 43:3, 5 + (see [ מָּנֶה‎] 2b).

b. see, with accusative of thing: subject עֵינַיִם עַיִן,‎ Josh 24:7 (E) 1Sam 24:11 (van d. H. Baer; v.24:10 Gi), Deut 3:21 5t. Deuteronomy, +; תִּרְאֶינָה אֶתעֵֿינָיו וְעֵינָיו‎ Jer 32:4, compare 34:3; accusative omitted 2Sam 24:3; Deut 21:7 9t. (לִרְאוֺת‎) 1Sam 6:13 read ᵐ5 לקְרָאתוֺ‎ We Dr Kit Bu HPS Now); subject pers Gen 13:15; 31:12 + very often; with accusative of congnate meaning with verb מַרְאֶה‎ Exod 3:8 7t., מַרְאָה‎ Dan 10:7 (twice in verse); 10:8, חָזוֺן‎ 8:15, חֶזְיֹנוֺת‎ Joel 3:1; hence see absolute= receive revelation, Isa 30:10 (|| חזה‎), compare Ezek 13:3 and see I. רֹאֶה‎; with accusative עֶרְוָה‎, see ׳צ‎, p. 788 f.; see war, i.e. see it impending Exod 13:17 (E); ר ׳וְאֶתהַֿלַּמִּידִים אֶתהַֿקּוֺתֹ‎ 20:18 (Gi 20:15); הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ רֹאֵי‎ Eccl 7:11 those who see the sun = living men; accusative of thing. omitted Exod 22:9; 2Sam 13:5 +, בֶּחָזוֺן וָאֶרֵאֶה‎ Dan 8:2 (twice in verse).(absolute); יֵדְעוּ לֹא יִרְאוּ וְלֹא‎ Neh 4:5; רֹאִים עֵינֵי‎ Isa 32:3, רֹאִים מְקוֺם‎ Job 34:26; with adverb or adverb phrase instead of accusative of thing: כָּהֵנָּה‎ Gen 41:19 compare Isa 66:8; Ezek 1:27 (twice in verse), כַּאֲשֶׁר‎ 2Kin 2:19; 2Chr 29:8; 30:7; Job 4:8; Ezek 16:50; Dan 1:13, כֵּן‎ Psa 48:9.

2 see, followed by accusative + clause or phrase of closer designation: (I) + epexegetical clause with כִּי‎, accusative of person Gen 6:2 saw them that they were fair, 12:4 (both J), Exod 2:2; 32:25 (both E), 1Kin 11:28, accusative of face + id. Gen 31:5 (E), Exod 34:25 (P); accusative of thing Gen 49:15 (poem), Isa 22:9; Gen 1:4 (P), Eccl 2:24; 4:4 and probably 2Kin 14:26 (reading הוּא מַר כִּי‎); (2) ׳ר וְעָמָ֑ד עָלָיו כָּלהַֿבָּא‎ 2Sam 20:12; (3) + adjective (including participle), accusative person Gen 7:1 (J), Amos 9:1; 2Sam 18:10 39t. (Jer 46:5 strike out ᵐ5 ׳ר‎ Gie), + accusative אֲשֶׁר‎ Exod 14:13 (twice in verse) (J); accusative of thing, 23:5; 33:10 (both E), Deut 22:4; Ezek 33:3, 6; Dan 1:10; 8:4, 6, 7; (4) + מָה‎, accusative of thing Num 13:18 (JE), Hag 2:3; (5) + preposition Phr., accusative of person Exod 5:19 (J), Zech 4:10; Eccl 10:7; Est 5:9; accusative of thing + בִּכְבוֺדוֺ‎ Hag 2:3, + כ‎ pres. Jer 23:13-14, + כ‎ person Judg 9:36, כ‎ of thing 2Sam 18:27; (6) accusative of person + adverb accusative + כ‎ person Jer 30:6.

3 see, so as to learn to know: with accusative of person Deut 33:9 (|| יַדַע הִכִּיר,‎); with accusative of thing 1:19, 31; 11:2; Job 11:11 (|| יָדַע‎ ), Psa 16:10; 49:10; = have experience of, Jer 5:12; 14:13; 20:18; 42:14; Zeph 3:15; Psa 89:49; Eccl 5:17, רֹאֶה אֵינֶנּוּ בְּעֵינָיו שֵׁנָה‎ 8:16; ראית מָה‎ Gen 20:10 i.e.what hast thou encountered, that . . . ? BacherZAW xix (1899). 345 ff.; Terminol. 177 f.

4 absolute see, have (power of) vision, Gen 27:1 (J), 48:10 (E), 1Sam 3:2; 4:15; 1Kin 14:4, miraculous 2Kin 6:17 (twice in verse); 6:20 (twice in verse); denied of idols Deut 4:28; Psa 115:5; 135:16; figurative of spiritual vision Isa 6:10; 29:18; 42:18; Jeremiah 5: Deut 29:3; Ezek 12:2 (twice in verse); Psa 40:13; 69:24; רֹאָה עַיִן‎ Prov 20:12. — 1Sam 14:27 read Qr see אור‎.

5 see = perceive:

a. followed by clause with כִּי‎, Exod 3:4; 8:11; Gen 1:10, 12 + often(1Sam 23:15 read וַיִּרָא‎ and he feared We Dr Kit Bu HPS Now); omit כִּי‎ (late) Lam 1:10; Psa 49:11; Eccl 3:16; followed by מָה‎ of indirect question Gen 2:19 (J), 37:20 (E), Judg 9:48; Deut 32:20; Jer 7:17; 33:24; Ezek 8:6; Jonah 4:5 +; בַּמָּה‎ Judg 16:5 compare 1Sam 14:38, כַּמָּה‎ Zech 2:6; Psa 35:17; followed by מִי‎ of indirect question 1Sam 14:17; Isa 40:26; Lam 2:20 ( + הַבִּיטָה‎); followed by אֵי‎ 1Sam 26:16, אֵיכֹה‎ 2Kin 6:13, אֵיפֹה‎ Jer 3:2; followed by clause with הֲ‎ whether, Gen 8:8; 18:21; Num 11:23 (all J), Exod 4:18 (E), Psa 14:2; 53:3; Song 6:11b Est 3:4, אִם‎ whether Jer 30:6; Lam 1:12; Psa 139:24; Cant 7:13, אֲשֶׁר‎ that or how 1Sam 18:15, אֵי‎ Eccl 2:3, שֶׁ‎ that 2:13, שְׁ‎ 3:18.

b. with accusative נַפְשׁוֺ צָרַת‎ Gen 42:21 (i.e. saw it by out-ward signs), compare Hosea 5:13. [Note, under

5 (rarely in other cases, and only Samuel Kings Jeremiah), Imperative + ידע‎ Imperative: וּרְאֵה דַּע‎ 1Sam 24:12; 2Sam 24:13; 1Kin 20:22; וּרְאִי דְּעִי‎ 1Sam 25:17; Jer 2:19; וּרְאוּ דְּעוּ‎ 1Sam 12:17; 14:38; 23:22; 1Kin 20:7; 2Kin 5:7; in reverse order, וּדְעוּ רְאוּ‎ 1Sam 23:23; Jer 5:1.]

6 look at, see, by direct volition:

a. subject men, with accusative of thing, Gen 9:22-23, (J), 42:9, 12 (E), Lev 13:3, 15 +; with accusative of land = reconnoitre Josh 2:1; look at sun, etc., for worship Deut 4:19; Job 31:26; = inspect 1Kin 9:12; Lev 14:36 (twice in verse); with accusative of person Num 24:20-21, (JE), Exod 2:25; Lev 13:3, 5 (all P), 1Sam 9:16 +, (19:15 HPS proposes אֶלבֵּֿית‎ for לִרְאוֺת‎); with preposition ׳ר רֹאִי אַחֲרִי‎ Gen 16:13 (J) I have looked after one seeing me (interpretation see Di).

b. subject God, with accusative of thing Gen 9:16 (P); = inspect 11:5 (J); look at with favour, accusative of person Job 37:24; Psa 138:6; so perhaps figurative, subject man, regard, with accusative אָוֶן‎ 66:18 (Hup-Now; Che Bae Dr and others intend); look with pleasure (accusative omitted, + מִן‎ by reason of, as a fruit of) Isa 53:11 (si vera); insert accusative ᵐ5 אוֺר‎ Houb Klo Du CheHpt Kit [perhaps], with Hiph`il ᵐ5 יַרְאֶה‎ Du CheHpt, rescues from travail his soul, makes it see light).

c. without accusative, look, take a look, etc. (of man and God; often + וְהִנֵּה‎ ), Gen 8:13; 18:2; Exod 3:2; Lev 13:8; Lam 3:50 (מִן‎ local), Gen 13:14 (מִן‎ local + ה‎ locative), Deut 3:27; Ezek 40:4; 44:5 (all בְּעֵינֶיךָ‎), + often; peculiarly, מִמֶּנִּי תַּעֲשׂוּ וְכֵן תִרְאוּ‎ Judg 7:17 (compare GFM).

d. look after, see after, learn about, with accusative of thing Gen 37:14 (J), with accusative of person = visit (go to see) 1Sam 15:35; 20:29; 2Sam 13:5-6, 2Kin 8:29 2Chr 22:6; 2Kin 9:16, compare Ezek 20:28, רֹאִי עֵין‎ Job 7:8 (Di Bu and others).

e. observe, watch, absolute, 1Sam 6:9, 16; 17:28; Eccl 8:16 (|| ידע‎).

f. look upon = endure to see, with accusative of thing Hab 1:13 (|| הִבִּיט‎).

g. look out, find out, accusative of person 2Kin 9:2; Gen 41:33 (E), + ל‎ person 1Sam 16:17; select, accusative of person + מִן‎ from among 2Kin 10:3, + ב‎ among + ל‎ person 1Sam 16:1; provide, furnish,, with accusative of thing Deut 33:21 (poem), + ל‎ person Gen 22:8 (E), compare absolute ׳י יִרְאֶה‎ as proper name, of a location = ׳י‎ seeth 22:14 a (E; ? read יֵרָאֶה‎, compare vb,

Niph`al and Di); רְאֻיוֺת‎ Est 2:9 looked out = suitable (as often Late Hebrew).

h. look at = concern oneself about, accusative of thing (+ בְּיָדוֺ‎) Gen 39:23 (J).

7 of mental observation:

a. Imperative see ! observe ! consider ! exclamation (nearly = הִנֵּה‎), followed by clause: Gen 27:27; 31:50 see ! God is witness 39:14; 41:41; Exod 4:21; Deut 1:8 +; followed by independent noun 2Sam 24:22 (|| 1Chr 21:23 followed by clause).

b. look at, i.e. inquire into, a matter, accusative of thing omitted, of ׳י‎, 1Sam 24:16 (Gi v.24:15).

c. give attention to, accusative of thing, Jer 2:31, absolute give attention ! 2Sam 13:28; 2Kin 6:32; Exod 25:40; Psa 45:11; take heed to, accusative of thing, 1Kin 12:16 2Chr 10:16; absolute take heed ! Exod 10:10, + מֶּן‎ 2Kin 10:23.

d. discern, ר ׳לִבִּי חָכְמָה‎ Eccl 1:16, ׳ר טוֺב‎ 3:13.

e. distinguish, with בֵּיןלְ֗֗֗‎ of person Mal 3:18.

f. consider, reflect, Eccl 7:14 (followed by clause oratio recta [direct speech]). 8. a. with ב‎, literally, look into, hence look at with interest (German 'sich vertiefen in'): (I) gaze at 1Sam 6:19 (on context see We Dr HPS), so as to become acquainted with Gen 34:1 (P); so as to find out Eccl 3:22; inspect liver (for omens) Ezek 21:26; some - what weakened = behold Job 3:9; 2Chr 7:3; Psa 64:9. (2) look at with kindness, of בָּעֳנִי ׳י,‎ Gen 29:32; 1Sam 1:11 ( + infinitive absolute), 2Sam 16:12, בַּצַּר‎ Psa 106:44. (3) upon a spectacle causing anger Exod 2:11 (E), grief Gen 21:16 (E), 44:34; Num 11:15 (both J), 2Kin 22:20 (subject עֵינָיִם‎) = 2Chr 34:28; Est 8:6 (twice in verse), abhorrence Isa 66:24. (4) gaze at with apprehension Eccl 11:4. (5) with joy, pleasure, 2Kin 10:16; Micah 7:9; Jer 29:32; Isa 52:8 (בְּעַיִן עַיִן‎, compare

Niph`al Num 14:14), Job 20:17; 33:28; Psalm 54:9; Psa 106:5; 128:5; Song 3:11; 6:11 a Eccl 2:1. (6) especially with exultation, triumph = feast eyes upon, sometimes gloat over (fallen enemies), Judg 16:27; Micah 7:10; Ezek 28:17; Obadiah 12, 13; Psa 22:18; 112:8; 118:7.

b. with אֶל‎ person Isa 17:7 (subject עֵינַיִם‎; || עַל שָׁעַה‎); עַל‎ person Exod 5:21 (J); עַלהָֿאָבְנָ֑יִם׳ר‎ 1:16 see [ אֹבֶן‎] and Comm., also SpiegelbZA xiv (June 1900), 269 ff.

c. with יִר ׳הָאָדָם יִר וְיוה ׳לַעֵינַיִם לַלֵּבָב ל,‎ 1Sam 16:7, יִרְאֶהלָּֿ֑מוֺ מִי‎ Psa 64:6. — Corrupt is הָאָדָם כְתוֺר וּרְאִיתַנִי‎ 1Chr 17:17 (and || הָאָדָם תּוֺרַת וְזֹאת‎ 2Sam 7:19), read וַתַּרְאֵנִי‎ (with other changes) We Dr Kau Bu HPS Now; Ezek 12:12 read probably

Niph`al ᵐ5‎ Hi Co Krae; Micah 6:9 read probably יִרְאָה‎ compare Now GASm.

Niph`al Perfect3masculine singular נִרְאָה‎ Gen 48:3 +, etc.; Imperfect3masculine singular יֵרָאֶה‎ 22:14 +, jussive יֵרָא‎ Exod 34:3; Lev 9:6, וַיֵּרָא‎ Gen 12:17 +; 1 singular וָאֵרָא‎ Exod 6:3, etc.; Imperative masculine singular הֵרָאֵה‎ 1Kin 18:1; Infinitive construct לְהֵרָאוֺת‎ 1Sam 17:17 +, לֵרָאוֺת‎ Isa 1:12 2t., הֵרָאֹה‎ Judg 13:21; 1Sam 3:21, etc.; —

1 appear, especially

a. of ׳י‎ (God): with אֶל‎ person Gen 12:7 (twice in verse) + 6 t. J, 35:1 (E), 35:9; 48:3; Exod 6:3 (ב שַׁדַּי, בְּאֵל‎ essent.), Lev 9:4 (all P), 1Kin 3:5; 9:2 (twice in verse) = 2Chr 7:12; 1Kin 11:9; with ל‎ person Jer 31:3; 2Chr 1:7; 3:1 (insert ᵐ5 ׳י‎ Kau Kit); absolute Gen 22:14 in the mountain where ׳י‎ appeareth (probably, Di StaG i. 450 Dr Hast. DB ii. 563; E), Num 14:14 (J E; בְּעַיִן עַיִן‎, see Isa 52:8 Qal 8 a (5)), Lev 16:2 (P; ב‎ location +עַל‎), 1Sam 3:21 (ב‎ location), 2Sam 22:11 (עַלכַּֿנְפֵירֿוּחַ‎; < וַיֵּדֶא‎ || Psa 18:11), + 5 t.; of י ׳מַלְאַךְ‎, with אֶל‎ person Exod 3:2 (E), Judges 13: of י ׳כְּבוֺד‎; with אֶל‎ person Lev 9:6, 23; Num 14:10 (ב‎ location), 16:19; 20:6 (all P), Judg 6:12; 13:3; עַל‎ person Isa 60:2; absolute Exod 16:10 (ב‎ location), Num 17:7 (both P).

גַּם‎768 adverb denoting addition, also, moreover, yea (Moabite id., also Zinjirli (Lzb250 Cooke166); probably akin to √ ; compare (accusative) in a mass, altogether) —

1 also, moreover, emphasizing sometimes the thought of an entire sentence, but more usually the word immediately following, as Gen 3:6 לְאִישָׁהּ גַּם וַתִּתֵּן‎ and gave also to her husband, Genesis 3:27 and take also of the tree of life, 7:3; 19:21; 24:19; 26:21; 29:27; 30:15; 32:21 (֗֗֗ הִגֵּה גַּם‎: so Est 7:9) Gen 48:11; Exod 8:28; 12:32b Deut 1:37; 1Sam 28:20; 2Sam 11:12; 2Kin 9:27; Isa 7:13 +. Often before pronouns, Gen 4:4 הוּא גַם הֵבִיא וְהֶבֶל‎ and Abel, he also brought, 20:5 וְהִיאגַֿםהִֿוא‎ (so only here) and she herself also, 20:6; 27:31 הוּא גַּם וַיַּעַשׂ‎, 30:8; Deut 3:20; Judg 3:31; 6:35; 9:19; 1Sam 19:20-24 Jer 12:6; 48:26 etc. (compare MI6 הא גם ויאמר‎): especially in Genealogies of J (BuUrg. 220) Gen 4:22, 26; 10:21; 19:38; 22:20, 24 compare Judg 8:31. גַּם‎ followed by pronoun also begins a sentence with emphasis in an elevated style, thou (they) also, Isa 14:10; Jer 12:6 (twice in verse); 48:7; Ezek 16:52; Nahum 3:11 (twice in verse). After a pronoun in an oblique case (Ges§ 135, 2) Gen 27:34; 1Sam 19:23; 2Sam 17:5; Jer 25:14; 27:7 +. וְגַם‎ and also (more often than גַּם‎ alone attaching a sentence) Gen 6:4; 14:16; 15:14; 17:16; 20:12; 24:14, 46; 30:6; 37:7; 38:24; 42:28; Exod 2:19; 3:9; 4:14; Josh 7:11 (5 t.) 1Sam 4:17; 1Kin 21:19 + often; with a negative = neither Exod 5:2; 34:3 and elsewhere — גַּם ֗֗֗ גַּם‎ (like et ... et) both ... and Gen 44:16; 47:3, 19; Num 18:3; Jer 51:12; Psa 49:3 +: גַּם ֗֗֗ גַּם ֗֗֗ גַּם‎ Gen 24:25; Judg 8:22; Eccl 9:6: with a negative neither ... nor Num 23:25; 1Sam 20:27; 1Kin 3:26, and (3t.) Gen 43:8; Exod 4:10; 1Sam 28:6. So (but seldom) גַּםוְ֗֗֗גַם‎ Gen 24:44; Exod 10:25f.; 1Sam 2:26; 12:14; 26:25: with negative 21:9. — N.B. In poetry independence and emphasis is sometimes given by גַּם‎ to a new idea, where in English we should be satisfied with and: Psa 107:5; 137:1; Job 24:19; Cant 7:14; Lam 4:15.

2 with stress on a particular word, even, Exod 4:9; Num 22:33 אוֺתְךָ גַּם‎ even thee I had slain, and kept her alive, 2Sam 17:10; Jer 2:33; Psa 132:12; Prov 14:13 even in laughter the heart is sorrowful, 14:20; 17:28; 20:11; Ruth 2:15; Nehemiah 3:35; and so often after כִּי‎, Deut 12:31 for even their sons they burn in the fire to their gods, 1Sam 22:17; Isa 26:12; Jer 6:11; 12:6; 14:5; Hosea 9:12 לָהֶם כִּיגַֿםאֿוֺי‎ for even woe is it to them when I depart from them; הֲגַם‎ Gen 16:13; 1Sam 10:11-12, = 19:24; 1Kin 17:20; Psa 78:20; Job 41:1; Est 7:8. Other cases: — 1Sam 24:12 רְאֵה גַּם רְאֵה‎ see, yea see ! (but HupQu. Job vi. רָאֹה גַּם‎: compare below) Psa 118:11; Job 2:10 נְקַבֵּל אֶתהַֿטּוֺב גַּם‎ shall we receive good (emphatic) from God and not evil ? 21:7; interposed once between a substantive and adjective Gen 20:4 Gentemne etiam justam interficies? emphasizing כֹּל‎, Deut 28:61; Judg 9:49b 1Sam 22:7 לְכֻלְּכֶם גַּםֿ‎ to all (emphatic) of you will he give ...? 2Sam 19:31 יִקָּ֑ח אֶתהַֿכֹּל גַּם‎ yea, the whole let him take! Isa 26:12; אֶחָד‎ 2Sam 17:12b and we will not leave ֗֗֗ אֶחָד גַּם‎ even one (similarly 17:13 b), Psa 14:3 (= 53:4) אֶחָד גַּם אֵין‎; an infinitive or cognate accusative attached to a verb, Gen 31:15; 46:4; Num 11:15; 16:13; 1Sam 1:6. שְׁנֵיהֶם גַּם‎ literally even both i.e. the one as well as the other (German alle beide) is said idiomatically, Gen 27:45 (שְׁנֵיכֶם‎), Deut 22:22; 23:19; 1Sam 25:43 (שְׁתֵּיהֶן‎), Prov 17:15; 20:10, 12; Ruth 1:5.

3 introducing a climax, yea, especially in a rhetorical style, Gen 27:33; Deut 23:3; 23:4; Judg 5:4 (twice in verse); Isa 13:3; 14:8; 43:13 yea, from to-day I am the same, 44:12 רָעֵב גַּם‎ yea, he is hungry, and has no strength, 47:3; 48:8 (3 t. in verse); 57:7; Jer 46:16; 48:2; 51:44; Hosea 7:9; Psa 41:10; 84:7; 139:12; Isa 66:8 אֶתבָּֿנֶיהָ צִיּוֺן גַּםיָָֽֿלְדָה, כִּיחָֿ֫לָה‎, Jer 5:28; 12:2; Ezek 24:5; Job 21:7; Song 8:1: emphasizing an extreme, or aggravated, case, yea, even, Isa 49:15 yea, these may forgot, Jer 8:17 yea, the stork knoweth, etc., Isa 23:12 שָׁם גַּם‎ even there no rest shall be for thee (so Psa 139:10), Isa 49:25; 57:6; Jer 23:11b; Mal 3:15; Psa 84:4.

4 expressing correspondence, especially in the matter of retribution (the גַּם‎ correlativum), so frequently אָנֹכִי גַּם אֲנִי, גַּם‎ I also (on my part): — Gen 20:6 I also [as well as thyself] know that thou hast done this innocently, Josh 24:18; Judg 2:21; 1Sam 1:28 (compare Dr) 28:22 אַתָּה גַּם‎ thou also (as I have done 28:21), 2Sam 12:13 ׳י‎ also [responding to thy confession] hath removed thy sin, 2Kin 2:3, 5; Isa 31:2; 66:3-4 (גם ֗֗֗ גם‎, emphasizing the action of both parties), Jer 2:36; 4:12 now will I also [in correspondence with their deeds] speak judgments with them, 7:11; 51:49 (גם ֗֗֗ גם‎), Ezek 5:8, 11; 16:43 (וְגַם‎ = therefore also), 23:35; Hosea 4:6 because thou hast forgotten the direction of thy God, I also (on my part) will forget thy children, Psa 52:7 (thou lovest evil, etc.) יִתָּצְךָ אֵל גַּם‎ God also (on his part) will pluck thee up, 71:22; 133:1; Prov 1:26; Job 7:11; 12:3; 16:4; so וְגַם‎ Judg 2:3; Amos 4:6-7, Micah 6:13; Mal 2:9. In the apodosis (uncommon): Gen 13:16 if a man could number the dust of the earth, יִמָּנֶה זַרְעֲךָ גַּם‎ thy seed also should be numbered, Jer 31:36-37, 33:21, 26; Zech 8:6. The correspondence is sometimes of the nature of a climax: Gen 27:33; 30:8 I have wrestled, יָכֹלְתִּי גַּם‎ (compare 1Kin 22:22 תּוּכָ֔ל וְגַם‎, Jer 50:24), Isa 66:8.

5 connecting two ideas which express (or imply) a contradiction, גַּם‎ acquires sometimes an adversative force (compare אַף‎ 1 end), yet, but, though: Psa 95:9 they tried me, but also (Che) saw my work (namely of judgment), 129:2; Jer 6:15 = 8:12; Ezek 20:23; Eccl 4:8, 16; 5:18; Neh 6:1. So וְגַם‎ Ezek 16:28; 20:15; Eccl 3:13; 6:7; Neh 5:8.

6 כִּי גַּם‎ (with imperfect) yea, when Lam 3:8, even when Prov 22:6; yea though (stating an imagined case) Isa 1:15; Hosea 8:10; 9:16; Psa 23:4 (so אִם גַּם‎ Eccl 8:17); also (is it) that Ruth 2:21 (see כִּי‎ 1d). גַם כִּי‎ = for even (see above 2); = though even, although (conceding a fact) Eccl 4:14 (see De) 8:12.

רבך.def:
H853. eth

I. אֵת‎, with makk. אֶתֿ‎, with suffix אֹתִי‎; אֹתְכָה אֹתְךָ,‎ Num 22:33, אֹתָ֑כָה אֹתָ֑ךְ,‎ Exod 29:35, feminine אֹתָךְ‎; אֹתוֺ‎ etc.; 2 plural אֶתְכֶם‎, once אוֺתְכֶם‎ Josh 23:15; 3masculine plural regularly אֹתָם‎, rarely אֶתְהֶם‎ Gen 32:1; Exod 18:20; Num 21:3; Ezek 34:12; 1Chr 6:50, once אוֺתְהֶם‎ Ezek 23:45; 3feminine plural, on the contrary, regularly אֶתְהֶן‎ (13 t.), once אֹתָן‎ 16:54 (also אוֺתְהֶן‎ 23:47, אֹתָ֖נָה‎ Exod 35:26, אוֺתָ֖נָה‎ Ezek 34:21); forms with cholem also often written plene: — the

mark of the accusative, prefixed as a rule only to nouns that are definite (Moabite id., Phoenician אית‎ i.e. אִיַּת‎ (Schrödp. 213 f.); Aramaic יָת‎ frequently in ᵑ7‎; Syriac very rare as mark of accusative (for which is preferred), but used often in the sense of substance οὐσία, also in that of self, e.g. per se, reapse, sibi ipsi, PS1640f., Samaritan ; Arabic , only used with suffix, when it is desired to emphasize the pronoun, e.g. Qor 1:4 WAG i. § 189. [Ethiopic uses k£y¹ similarly, Di§ 150 a; but it is dubious if this is etymologically akin.] The primitive form will have been 'iwyath, originally a substantive with following Genitive, Olp. 432; whether ultimately a parallel development with אוֺת‎ sign from √ אוה‎ is uncertain: Ol WAG i. § 188 LagM i. 226 affirm, NöZMG 1886, 738 doubts. In Hebrew the ground-form is אוֺת‎; the forms with ¢, e being abbreviated. In post Biblical Hebrew, used in combination with another preposition: thus הַיּוֺם בְּאוֺתוֺ‎ = Bibl. הַשָּׁעָה בְּאוֺתָהּ הַהוּא, בַּיּוֺם‎; or as a nomin., e.g. הָאִישׁ אוֺתוֺ‎ = Bibl. הַהוּא הָאִישׁ‎).

1 As mark of the accusative prefixed to substantives defined either by the article (or כֹּל‎), or by a Genitive or pronominal affix, or in virtue of being proper names:

a. with transitive verbs, Gen 1:1, 16, 29, 30; 2:11; 4:1-2, 9:3 (אֶתֿכֹּל׃‎) etc. Similarly אֶתמִֿי‎ whom (in particular), Josh 24:15; 1Sam 12:3; 28:11; Isa 6:8 and elsewhere (but never אֶתמָֿה‎); also with זֶה‎ Gen 29:33; 44:29; 1 Samuel 21:16; 1Kin 22:27 +, זֹאת‎ Gen 29:27; 2Sam 13:27 +, אֵלֶּה‎ Gen 46:18; Lev 11:18; Isa 49:21 +. So pretty uniformly in prose; but in poetry את‎ is commonly dispensed with. By the use of את‎ with the pronominal affix, a pronoun can at once, if required, be placed in a position of emphasis; let the order of words from this point of view be carefully noticed in the following passages: Gen 7:1; 24:14; 37:4; Lev 10:17; 11:33; Num 22:32 thee I had slain, and her I had kept alive, Deut 4:14; 6:13, 23; 13:5; Judg 14:3 לִי קַח אוֺתָהּ‎ take for me her, 1Sam 14:35; 15:1; 18:17; 21:10 קָ֔ח תִּקַּחלְֿךָ אִםאֹֿתָהּ‎ if thou wilt take that, take it, 1Kin 1:35; 14:9; Isa 43:22; 57:11; Jer 9:2. So הַאוֺתִי‎ 5:22; 7:19. It also sometimes enables the reflexive sense to be expressed (elsewhere נַפְשָׁם‎) 7:19; Ezek 34:2. Rarely with a substantive which is undefined (Ew§ 277 d 2 Ges§ 117, 1, R. 2), as Exod 21:28; Num 21:9; Lev 20:14; 1Sam 24:6 (but see Dr) 2Sam 4:11; 18:18; 23:21; or which, though definite, is without the article, Gen 21:30; 2Sam 15:16; Lev 26:5; 1Sam 9:3 (so Num 16:15) Isa 33:19; 41:7; Ezek 43:10 (for further examples see Ew 1.c.)

b. with a passive verb (Ges§ 121. 1 Ew§ 295 b) conceived as expressing neutrally the action in question, and construed accordingly with an accusative of that which is its real object: examples occur with tolerable frequency from Gen 4:18 (J) אֶתעֿירָד לַחֲנוֺךְ וַיִּוָּלֵד‎, 17:5 (P), אַברָם אֶתשִֿׁמְךָ עוֺד יִקָּרֵא לֹא‎ there shall not be called (=one shall not call) thy name Abram, 21:5 (E), 27:42; 2Sam 21:11; 1Kin 18:13; Hosea 10:6 etc., to Jer 35:18; 38:4; 50:20; Ezek 16:4-5, Est 2:13 (compare DrJPh xi. 227 f.): also with passive verbs of filling (Ew§ 281 b), as Exod 1:7 +.

c. with neuter verbs or expressions, especially such as involve the idea of regarding, or treating, appy. by a construction κατὰ σύνεσιν (rare), Josh 22:17; 2Sam 11:25; Neh 9:32 (compare 1Sam 20:13 Dr). Once after אֵין‎, Hag 2:17; אֵלַיָֽ אֶתְכֶם אֵין‎.

d. poet. (si vera lectio), after an abstract noun used with a verbal force, Hab 3:13 (Amos 4:11; Isa 13:19; Jer 50:40 מַהְמֵּכָה‎ exerts a verbal force, like the Arabic nom. verbi [see WAG i. § 196, 43]; and Num 10:2; Ezek 17:9 לְמַשְׂאוֺת לְמַסַּע,‎ are Aramaizing infinitives: compare Ew§ 239 a).

2 את‎ marks an accusative in other relations than that of direct object to a verb: a. with verbs of motion (very rare) Num 13:17; Deut 1:19; 2:7 (to 'walk the wilderness'); denoting the goal Judg 19:18; Ezek 21:25 (Ew§ 281 d, n., 282 a 1). b. denoting time (duration), also very rare: Exod 13:7; Lev 25:22; Deut 9:25. c. expressing the accus. of limitation (rare): Gen 17:11, 14; 1Kin 15:23.

3 Chiefly in an inferior or later style, אֵת‎ (or וְאֵת‎) is used irregularly, partly (α), as it would seem, to give greater definiteness (so especially וְאֵת‎) at the mention of a new subject (when it may sometimes be rendered as regards), or through the influence of a neighbouring verb (a construct κατὰ σύνεσιν), or by an anacoluthon, partly (β) as resuming loosely some other preposition Thus (α) Exod 1:14; Num 3:26, 46; 5:10 (with הָיָה‎: so Ezek 35:10) Num 18:21b Deut 11:2 (anacoluthon), 14:13; Josh 17:11; Judg 20:44, 46 (contr. 20:25; 20:35) 1Sam 17:34 (see Dr) 26:16; 2Sam 21:22; 2Kin 6:5; Isa 53:8 (probably), 57:12; Jer 23:33 (but read rather with הַמַּשָּׂא אַתֶּם ᵑ9 ᵐ5‎) 27:8; 36:22; 38:16 Kt, 45:4 b Ezek 16:22; 17:21; 20:16; 29:4; b 43:7 (ᵐ5‎ Co prefix הֲרָאִיתָ‎) 44:3; Zech 8:17; Eccl 4:3; Dan 9:13; Neh 9:19, 34; 1Chr 2:9; 2Chr 31:17. In 1Sam 30:23; Hag 2:5 probably some such word as remember is to be understood. (β) Jer 38:9; Ezek 14:22; b 37:19 b Zech 12:10; אֵת סָבִיב‎ 1Kin 6:5; Ezek 43:17 strangely (in 1Kings ᵐ5‎ omits the clause: so StaZAW 1883, 135). — In 1Kin 11:1 וְ‎ is merely and also, and especially (see וְ‎); 11:25 is corrupt (read with הֲדָד עָשָׂה אֲשֶׁר הָרָעָה זֹאת ᵐ5‎); Ezek 47:17-18, 19 read similarly for זֹאת ואת,‎: see 47:20. — For some particulars as to the use of את‎, see A. M. WilsonHebraica. vi. 139 ff. 212 ff. (who, however, confuses it sometimes with II. אֵת‎). For denoting the pronominal object of a verb, את‎ with suffix preponderates relatively much above the verbal affix in P, as compared with J E Deuteronomy Judges Samuel Kings (see GieZAW 1881, 258 f.), — partly, probably, on account of the greater distinctness and precision which P loves.

יָת‎ mark of accusative (= Biblical Hebrew I. אֵת‎; Palmyrene ית‎; ZinjirliHad. 28 with suffix ותה‎; Nabataean, Palmyrene with suffix יתה‎ (Lzb263 Cooke170; compare RÉS468); ᵑ7‎ Samaritan יָת‎; Syriac (rare)); — Dan 3:12 יָָֽתְהוֺן מַנִּיתָ דִּי‎ whom thou hast appointed.

לָשׁוֺן‎ noun masculineJosh 7:21 and (more often) feminineIsa 28:11 tongue (Late Hebrew id.; also Assyrian lišânu; Arabic ; Ethiopic ; Aramaic לִישָּׁן לִשָּׁן,‎, (all li-); Zinjirli לשן‎ DHMSendsch. 59); — absolute ׳ל‎ Exod 4:10 +; הַלָּשֹׁן‎ Josh 15:2; construct לְשׁוֺן‎ 7:21 +; suffix לְשׁוֺנִי‎ 2Sam 23:2; לְשֹׁנוֺ‎ Exod 11:7 2t.; לְשׁוֺנוֺ‎ Judg 7:5; Est 1:22; לְשׁוֺנְךָ‎ Psa 34:14; לְשׁוֺנְכֶם‎ Isa 59:3, etc.; plural לְשֹׁנוֺת‎ absolute Psa 31:21; Isa 66:18; construct Zech 8:23; suffix לְשֹׁנֹתָם‎ Gen 10:20, 31; —

a. used in lapping Judg 7:5; cleaving to the palate (חֵק‎), in thirst Lam 4:4, so as to produce dumbness Job 29:10 (|| נֶחְבָּא קוֺל‎), Psa 137:6; Ezek 3:26 (|| נֶאֱלַם‎); cleaving to jaws (מַלְקוֺחַ‎) Psa 22:16; ׳ל נָשָׁ֑תָּה בַּצָּמָא‎ Isa 41:17 their tongue for thirst is parched; ׳לְ בְּפִיהֶם תִּמַּק‎ Zech 14:12 (of ׳י‎s judgment); a choice morsel is held ל ׳תַּחַת‎ Job 20:12 (figurative of mischief), compare Psa 10:7 (ready to be uttered), 66:17 (|| מֶּה‎), Song 4:11.

b. usually as organ of speech, both good and bad (especially Psalms, Proverbs, often || שָׂפָה מֶּה,‎); — ל ׳כְּבַד‎ Exod 4:10 (J) heavy of tongue; ל ׳מַעֲנֵה‎ Prov 16:1, עַללְֿשׁוֺנִי מִלָּתוֺ‎ 2Sam 23:2, compare Prov 31:26; Psa 139:4 (׳בִּל‎), עַוְלָה בִּלְשׁוֺנִי הֲיֵשׁ‎ Job 6:30; ל בְּיַד וְחַיִּים ׳מָוֶת‎ Prov 18:21, compare 21:23; 25:15; of (false) prophets, ל ׳הַלֹּקְהִים‎ Jer 23:31; subject of verb of speaking, בֶּר‎ Di — לְשׁוֺנִי דִּבְּרָה בִחִכִּי‎ Job 33:2; Psa 12:4; 37:30; compare (Jer 9:7 below and) לְדַבֵּר ׳ל תְּמַהֵר ֗֗֗‎ Isa 32:4, מָהִיר סֹפֵר עֵט לְשׁוֺנִי‎ Psa 45:2, i.e. as swift as a rapid scribe's stylus; subject of הָגָה‎ Isa 59:3; Job 27:4; Psa 35:28; 71:24; subject of נִשְׁבַּע‎ Isa 45:23; ׳ל בָּאָרֶץ תִּהַלַךְ‎ Psa 73:9; of hostile speech, insolence, etc., Josh 10:21 (J E; object of I. חָרַץ‎ q. v., compare

3 below), Jer 18:18; Isa 3:8; ל ׳זַעַם‎ Hosea 7:16 (but text dubious, compare We Now), ׳ל חַדָּה חֶרֶב‎ Psa 57:6, compare 64:4; ל שָֽׁנְנוּ ׳נָחָשׁ כְּמוֺ‎ 140:4; ׳כָּללֿ אִתָּךְ תָּקוּם‎ Isa 54:17; ל ׳הֶאֱרִיךְ‎ 57:4; further, Jer 9:2; 9:4; as instrument of seductive flattery (הֶחֱלִיק‎), without בְּ‎, Psa 5:10; Proverbs 28:33, compare לָ חֶלְקַת ׳נָכְרִיָּה‎ Prov 6:24;. of falsehood Psa 78:36 (compare below); of slander (compare לושֵׁן‎) עַללֿ ׳רָגַל‎ 15:3, לָשׁוֺן אִישׁ‎140:12, compare ׳לְ סָ֑תֶר‎ Proverbs 25:33; בְּל ׳חָטָא‎ 39:2; compare 64:9 (text dubious, see Hup Che Bae); moral qualities ascribed to: — as arrogant 12:5 (compare 12:4 above); as devising injuries, ל תַּחְשֹׁב ׳הַוּוֺת‎ 52:4, compare ׳לְ הַוֺת‎ Prov 17:4; ׳ל מִרְמָה תַּצְמִיד‎ Psa 50:19 nectere fraudem; ל נְצֹר ׳מֵרָ֑ע‎ 34:14 ׅ‎ || מִרְמָה מִדַּבֵּר (וּשְׂפָתֶיךָ‎; often of lying tongue: שֶׁקֶר לְשׁוֺן‎ Prov 6:17; 12:19; 21:6; 26:28; Psa 109:2; ׳לְ מִרְמָה‎ 52:6; ׳לָ רְמִיָּה‎ Micah 6:12; Psa 120:2; 120:3; ׳לְ תַּרְמִית‎ Zeph 3:13; ׳לְ תַּהְמֻּכוֺת‎ Prov 10:31, and בִּל ׳נֶהְמָּךְ‎ 17:20; עֲרוּמִים׳ל‎ Job 15:5; also ׳ל דִּבֵּ֑ר מִרְמָה‎ Jer 9:7; on the other hand ׳לְ צַדִּיק‎ Prov 10:20; ׳ל חֲכָמִים‎ 12:18; 15:2; לָ ׳מַרְמֵּה‎ 15:4; ׳לְ לִמּוּדִים‎ Isa 50:4. — Note phrases ל ׳שׁוֺט‎ Job 5:21 scourge of (the) tongue, לְשֹׁנוֺת רִיב‎ Psa 31:21; לְשׁוֺנָם מַּלַּג‎ 55:10: also הַלּ ׳בַּעַל‎ Eccl 10:11 (of serpent-charmer), and ל עַלשְֿׂפַת ׳וַתֵּעֲלוּ‎ Ezek 36:3. — On tongue of ׳י‎ (once), see 4 below

c. organ of singing, subject of רָנַן‎ Psa 51:16; 126:2; Isa 35:6, עָנָה‎ Psa 119:172.

(V. above as in Syriac, the י‎ may not have been fully sounded: the Masoretes direct אַתְּ‎ to be everywhere read.)

אָ֑תְּ אַתְּ,‎ pronoun 2 singular feminine thou (feminine) (shortened from אַתִּי‎ (q. v.); in Syriac the two Genders are written differently, , , but, the not being sounded, are pronounced alike: in ᵑ7‎ both are written אַתְּ‎ or אַנְתְּ‎) Gen 12:11, 13; 24:23 +? Num 11:15; Deut 5:24; Ezek 28:14 used as a masculine (as in Aramaic of ᵑ7‎); but probably אַתָּ‎ (see below אַתָּה‎) should be here read.

H4480. min

or minni or minne מִןֿ‎ and מִּ ‎, before יְ‎ (except Dan 12:2; 2Chr 20:11) contracted to מִי‎ (as מִידֵי‎ from מִיְּדֵי‎), before guttural and ר‎, mostly מֵ‎, occasionally מִ‎ (Ges§ 102, l R.; more fully Köii. 291ff), מִן‎ before article in all books much commoner than -מֵ‎; מִן‎; before other words most frequently in Chronicles [51 t.: elsewhere 47 t. (Kö292)]; in poetry also מִנִּי‎, with the old י‎ of the Genitive (Ges§ 90.3a) Judg 5:14 (twice in verse); Isa 46:3 (twice in verse); Psa 44:11; 44:19; 68:32; 74:22; 78:2; 78:42; 88:10 19t. Job, and in לְמִנִּי‎ Micah 7:12 (twice in verse) and מִנֵּיֿ‎ (on analogue of עֲלֵי עֲדֵי,‎) Isa 30:11 (twice in verse), preposition expressing the idea of separation, hence out of, from, on account of, off, on the side of, since, above, than, so that not (Phoenician מ‎; Aramaic ; Arabic >; Ethiopic ; Sabean בן‎ (DHMZMG xxix.606 ff.; xxxvii.375)); with suff, מִמֶּנִּי‎ (the מִן‎ reduplicated, Ol§ 223c, and others, Köii. 289 f.), in poetry מִנִּי‎ 22:4; 30:1; 38:12; Job 16:6, מֶ֫נִּי‎ Psa 18:23; 65:4; 139:19; Job 21:16; 22:18; 30:10; מִמֵּךְ מִמֶּ֑ךָּ, מִמְּךָ,‎; מִמֶּ֫נּוּ‎ ( 4:12 מֶ֫נְהוּ‎), מִמֶּ֫נָּה‎; 1 plural מִמֶּ֫נּוּ‎ (according to Orientals מִמֵּ֫נֿוּ‎: see BaerJob. p. 57 Kö290); מִכֶּם‎; מֵהֶם‎ (מִנְּהֶם‎ 11:20), מֵהֵ֫מָּה‎ Jer 10:2; Eccl 12:12; מֵהֵ֫נָּה‎7t. (see הֵ֫מָּה‎ 8c), מֵהֶן‎ (editions מֵהֵן‎) Ezek 16:47, 52 (see ZerweckHeb, Präp. Min, 1894): — 1. with verbs expressing (or implying) separation or removal, whether from a person or place, or in any direction, also from guilt, calamity, etc.: — thus

a. to descend from a mountain Exod 19:14, to fall from a roof Deut 22:8, from heaven Isa 14:12, to go up from a valley Josh 10:7, to raise up from the dunghill 1Sam 2:8, or the ground 2Sam 12:17. So constantly with verbs of going, as ברח שׁב, הלך, בא,‎ (followed by a person, usually מפני‎), of calling, as Isa 24:14 מִיָּם צָֽהֲלוּ‎, 42:10-11, Psa 148:1 of asking or exacting as נָקַם דרשׁ, בקשׁ, שׁאל,‎,הִנָּקֵם‎, of delivering, as הציל הושׁיע,‎, etc., of hiding as העלים נעלם,‎, etc., of taking or withholding, as מנע חשׂך, לקח,‎, of keeping (from), as שׁמר נצר,‎, of being far, or desisting, as רחק‎ Exod 23:7, מִמֶּנּוּ חֲדַל‎ desist from us,14:2, so הֶרֶף‎ Deut 9:14,הֵנִיחַ‎ 12:10, השׁקיט‎ > Psa 94:13, שׁבת‎ Gen 2:2, compare 5:29; note especially the pregnant constructions, שׁפט‎ to judge (and save) from Psa 43:1, followed by מִיַּד‎ 1Sam 24:16 +, ענה‎ to answer (and save) from Psa 22:22, חרשׁ‎ and חשׁה‎ to be silent (turning) from 28:1 (twice in verse), ממני החרישׁו‎ Job 13:13; Jer 38:27; Psa 18:22 מאלהי רשׁעתי ולא‎ not did wickedly (turning) from my God, 30:4 Kt., 73:27, ממך כלזֿוֺנֶה‎, Jer 3:20 מִן בָּגַד‎ (ᵐ5‎ εἰς = ב‎), 31:13 with שִׂמַּח‎ (2Chr 20:27), Ezek 27:34; Prov 25:17; רֵעֶ֫ךָ מִבֵּית רַגְלְךָ הֹקַר‎, Isa 29:4; 63:17; Joel 1:12; Jer 51:5 מֵאֱלֹהָיו אַלְמָן‎ widowed (and severed) from etc., Ezek 44:22; also Judg 7:17 תַּעֲשׂוּ וְכֵן תִרְאוּ מִמֶּנִּי‎ ye shall see from me, i.e. learn what to do by observing me. Some of the verbs mentioned above are construed more precisely with מֵעַל מֵעִם, מֵאֵת,‎, q. v.: and others, especially מִּלֵּט מּדה, הצּיל, הושׁיע, דרשׁ, לקח,‎, idiomatic with מִיַּד‎. With infinitives, see below 7b. often also with adverbs, as מִשָּׁם‎ thence, מֵאַיִן‎ whence ? מִמֹּה מִוֶּה,‎ hence. compare also מִן חָפְשִׁי‎ free (safe) from Job 3:19, מִצָּרָיו עֵזֶר‎ a help from his foes Deut 33:7; Nahum 3:11 מֵאוֺיֵב מָעוֺז‎, Psa 32:7 מִצַּר סֵתֶר‎, Psalm 60:13 מִצָּ֑ר עֶזְרָת‎, Isa 4:6 מֵחֹרֶב צֵל‎ a shadow from, the heat, 25:4. Here also belong 40:15 מִדְּלִי מַר‎ a drop from (hanging from) a bucket; Song 4:1 goats גלעד מהר שֶׁגָָּֽלְשׁוּ‎ that sit up (seeming to hang) from the hills of Gilead (compare Od. 21. 420 ἐκ διφροιο καθήμενος: also the Arabic idiom , literally to be near from a thing): probably also the difficult passage Dan 8:9, and from one of them there came forth אַחַת קֶרֶן מִצְּעִירָה‎ a horn from (being) a little one, i.e. gradually increasing from small beginnings (but ? read צְעִירָה אַחֶרֶת‎ Bev compare 7:8).

b. מן‎ also, without a verb of similar significance, sometimes expresses the idea of separation, away from, far from (compare II. 2. 162 φίλης ἀπὸ πατρίδος αἴης): Prov 20:3 מֵרִיב שֶׁכֶת‎ to sit away from strife (compare ap. De), Num 15:24 if the thing be done הָעֵדָה מֵעֵינֵי‎ away from the eyes of etc., Judg 5:11 De RV (but Be RVm because of), Isa 14:19 cast out מִקִּבְרְךָ‎ away from thy sepulchre, Job 28:4 מֵאֱנוֺשׁ דַּלּוּ‎, Gen 4:11 cursed art thou מןֿ האדמה‎, De Di away from the (tilled) soil, compare 4:14 (but Kn Ke from, compare 4:12 a), 27:39 (probably) מִשְׁמַנֵּי הָאָרֶץ‎ away from the fatness of the earth shall be thy dwelling; almost = without, Job 11:15 then shalt thou lift up thy face מִמּוּם‎ away from, without spot, 19:26 (probably) מִבְּשָׂרִי‎ without my flesh shall I see God, 21:9 מִמַּחַד שָׁלוֺם בָּֽתֵּיהֶם‎ are at peace without fear, Prov 1:33; Jer 48:45 fleeing מִכֹּחַ עָֽמְדוּ‎ they stand without strength, Isa 22:3 אֻסָּ֫רוּ מִקֶּשֶׁת‎ (Hi De Di Che) they were bound without the bow (being used) (but Ges as

2e: by the bowmen), Zeph 3:18. (On 2Sam 13:16 see We or Dr). See also

7b. with of position, off, on the side of, on, especially with reference to quarters of the heavens (compare πρὸς Νότου, ἐκ δεξιῶν, a fronte, a tergo, etc.): Gen 2:8 ׳י‎ planted a garden in Eden מִקֶּדֶם‎ off, on the east, 12:8 וְהָעַי מִיָּם בֵּיתְאֵל מִקֶּדֶם‎ Bethel off (on) the West and `Ai off (on) the East; so מִנֶּגֶכ מִצָּפוֺן, מִמִּוְרָח,‎ Josh 11:3; 15:8; 18:5; 1Sam 14:5, etc.: similarly מִיָּמִין‎ on the right, מִשְּׂמאֹול‎ on the left, מִמּוּל‎ and (more rarely) מִמָּנִים‎ on the front, מֵאָחוֺר‎ = behind (2Sam 10:9), מִסָּבִיב‎ Deut 12:10 + round about, מִלְמַעְלָה מִמַּעַל,‎, and מֵעָ֑ל‎ (rare) = above, מִתַּחַת‎ Exod 20:4 + beneath, מִבַּיִת‎ on the inside, מִחוּץ‎ on the outside Gen 6:14 +, מִנֶּגֶד‎ in front, at a distance, 21:16 +, מֵרָחוֺק‎ Exod 2:4 + afar off, מִמְּנִ֫ימָה‎ within, מִזֶּהמִ֗֗֗וֶּה‎ and ֗֗֗ מִמֹּה מִמֹּה‎ on this side . . . on that side. And so even with verbs of motion, as Gen 11:2 בנסעם ויהי מִקֶּדֶם‎ as they journeyed — not from, but — on, the side of the east, virtually = eastwards, 13:11 and Lot journeyed מקדם‎ east, Isa 17:13; 22:3 מֵרָחוֺק ברחו‎ they fled — not from afar but — afar, 23:7 whose feet used to carry her מֵרָחוֺק‎ afar off to sojourn, 57:9 thou didst send thy messengers עדמֿרחוק‎ even to afar. With a following לְ‎ (or suffix), most of these words are frequently in the sense of on the east (west, etc.) of . . ., as Josh 8:13 מִיָּם לָעִיר‎ on the west of the city, לְ מִקֶּדֶם‎ Gen 3:24, לְ מִצְּפוֺן‎ (construct Ges§ 130 a, n.) Josh 8:11, 13; 24:30, מִימִינֶ֑ךָ‎ Psa 91:7, לְ מִתַּחַת‎ Gen 1:7, לְ מִמַּעַל‎ 22:9, לְ מִבֵּית‎ Lev 16:2: מֵאַחֲרֵי‎ behind Exod 14:19 בֵּיתְאֵל מִצַּד‎ beside Bethel Josh 12:9, מִצִּדּוֺ‎ beside it 1Sam 6:8, לַיַּרְדֵּן מֵעֵבֶר‎ on the other side of Jordan Num 21:1 +; לְ מֵהָֽלְאָה‎ beyond Amos 5:27; tablets written עֶבְרֵיהֶם מִשְּׁנֵי‎ on both their sides, מִכָּלעֲֿבָרָיו‎ Jer 49:32 + (see further the words cited). So מֵהַבַּיִת‎ on the side of the house Ezek 40:7-8, 9, מֵאֵצֶל‎ beside 40:7; 1Sam 20:21 the arrows are וָהֵנָּה מִמְּךָ‎ from thee and hither = on this side of thee, 20:22 וָהָֽלְהָא מִמְּךָ‎, compare Num 32:19 (twice in verse).

2 Out of, Greek ἐκ, Latin ex: thus

a. מִמִּצְרַיִם‎ out of Egypt: so (a) with verbs of proceeding, removing, expelling, etc., as יָצָא הוֺצִיא,‎ (see יָצָא‎), שִׁלַּח‎ Gen 3:23, לָקַח‎ 34:26, גָנַב‎ 40:15, הִכְרִית‎ Exod 8:5; Psa 101:8, גֵּרֵשׁ‎ Judg 11:7, etc.; to draw out of water, a pit, etc. Exod 2:10; Psa 40:3; to cast out of the hand Judg 15:17; to rescue out of the mouth Amos 3:12; to drink מִכּוֺס‎ 2Sam 12:3; Deut 30:3 מִןהָֿעַמִּים וְקִבֶּצְךָ‎, Ezek 11:17; 36:24 +: pregnantly with חָרֵד‎ Hosea 10:10-11, רגז‎ Micah 7:17 to tremble (and come) out of, חרג‎ Psa 18:46 (|| 2Sam 22:46 חגר‎), 2Sam 74:11; Isa 38:17 חָשַׁק‎ (ni חָשַׂךְ‎ leg.), Ezek 28:16 חִלֵּל‎, Ezra 2:62; compare מִמֶּה נִשְׁכַּח‎ Deut 31:21, מִלֵּב‎ Psa 31:13. In this application, often made more definite by the use of ֗֗֗ מִקֶּרֶב , ֗֗֗ מִתּוֺךְ‎ out of the midst of. (b) of the place out of which one looks, speaks, exerts power, etc., Gen 4:10; Num 24:19 (Psa 110:1), Deut 4:35 אתֿ השׁמיעך מןהֿשׁמים קלו‎, Amos 1:2 ׳י ישׁאג מציון‎, Psa 14:2; 20:3 send thee help מִקֹּדֶשׁ‎, 14:7 קָדְשׁוֺ מִשְּׁמֵי יַעֲנֵהוּ‎, 42:7; Psalm 68:36; 85:12; 109:10 מחרבזתיהם ודרשׁו‎ seek (their bread) out of their desolate homes (but Ew De as

1b far from; ᵐ5‎ Gr Che יְגָֹֽרְשׁוּ‎ let them be driven from), Psa 128:5; 130:1; Job 27:23; Isa 29:18 to see out of darkness, Song 2:9 to look out מִןהַֿחַלֹּנוֺת‎ from the windows (usually בעד‎), 5:4 he put forth his hand מִןהַֿחוֺר‎ from (i.e. in through) the hole (in the door or wall). (c) with בָּחַר‎ to choose out of, Exod 18:25 +?הִבְדִּיל‎ Deut 29:20; 1Kin 8:53,with יָדַע‎ Amos 3:2; Exod 19:5 ye shall be to me מכלהֿעמים סְגֻלָּה‎ a treasure (chosen) out of all peoples (compare with בָּחַר‎ Deut 7:6; 14:2).

b. of the material out of which anything is formed, or from which it is derived: (a) Gen 2:19 to form מןהֿאדמה‎ out of the soil, 2:23 וּבָשָׂר מֵעֲצָמַי עֶצֶם מִבְּשָׂרִי‎, Exod 39:1; Num 6:4; Hosea 13:2 to make images מִכַּסְמָּם‎, Psa 16:4 מִדָּם נִסְכֵּיהֶם‎, 45:14; Song 3:9; Isa 40:17 נחשׁבולֿו ותהו מאפס‎ as made of nought and unreality are they reckoned by him (|| נֶגְדּוֺ כְּאַיִן‎), 41:24 מֵאַיִן אַתֶּם הֵן‎ (|| מֵאָ֑פַע‎, read מֵאָ֑פֶם‎), Psa 62:10 מֵהֶבֶל‎ (al. 6c), Prov 13:11; Exod 25:19, 31 its cups, its knops, etc., יהיו ממנה‎ shall be from it (i.e. of one piece with it), so 25:35; 25:36; 27:2; 30:2 al.; (b) with verbs of eating, filling, etc., as שׁתה‎ Gen 9:21; Job 21:20 יִשְׁתֶּה שַׁדַּי מֵחֲמַת‎, Song 8:2 רָוָה הִשְׁקָה,‎ Psa 36:9 +, רִוָּה‎ Isa 34:7, שׂבע‎ Prov 18:20 +, השׂביע‎ Psalm 81:17 +, מִלֵּא‎ (rare) Psa 127:5: compare Deut 32:42 מִדָּם חִצַּי אַשְׁכִּיר‎, Isa 51:21; Psa 28:7 (peculiar) אֲהוֺדֶנּוּ וּמִשִּׁירִי‎ out of song I will thank him (69:31 ׳ב‎), also (unusual) Isa 2:3 מִדְּרָכָיו וְיוֺרֵנוּ‎ i.e. out of (the treasure of) his ways (al. particle = some of), Psa 94:12b תְלַמְּדֶנּוּ מִתּוֺרָֽתְךָ‎; Eccl 7:10 to speak מֵחָכְמָה‎ (compare Rabb מִתּוֺךְ‎).

c. of the source or origin: namely (a) of parents, Gen 16:2 ממנה אִבָּנֶה‎ I shall be built up out of her (so 30:3), 17:16 יהיו ממנה עמים מלכי‎, 35:11a: often of coming forth מִבֶּטֶן‎ Job 1:21, מֵחֲלָצֶיךָ‎ Gen 35:11b, ממעיך‎ 15:4, Isa 2:20 ׳י‎ give thee seed from this woman; compare Job 16:4 מִטָּמֵא טָהוֺר יִתֵּן מִי‎ (b) of the tribe or people, from which a person comes (compare 1a), Num 3:12 ישׂר מכני ֗֗֗ בכור ׳כל‎, Josh 12:4; 2Sam 4:2; 21:2; Jer 1:1 +; and so of a person's native place, as Judg 12:8 לחם מבית אבצן‎ Ibzan from Biblical, 13:2 מִצָּרְעָה אִישׁ‎ 17:1, 7; 1Sam 1:1; 9:1; 2Sam 23:20, 30; Amos 1:1 +, compare Jer 46:25 מִנּאֹ אָמוֺן‎; Isa 48:1 יָצָֽאוּ יְהוּדָה וּמִמֵּי‎, 48:2 נִקְראוּ הַקֹּדֶשׁ מֵעִיר‎, 58:12 מִמֵךְ וּבָנוּ‎ (those) from thee shall build, Psa 68:27 ישׂראל מִמְּקוֺר‎ ye (sprung) from the fountain of Israel, Micah 5:1; Nahum 1:11 1:14 figurative מִשִּׁמְךָ‎), Zeph 3:18; Jer 30:21; Zech 10:4. (c) of beasts and things, Gen 2:7 מִןהָֿאֲדָמָה עָפָר‎, Jer 5:6 מִיַּעַר אַרְיֵה‎ a lion from the woods, Psa 80:14 מִיַּעַרִ חֲזִיר‎; compare 10:18 מִןהָֿאָרֶץ אֶנוֺשׁ‎ man from the earth (terrenus), 72:16 מֵעִיר יָצִיצוּ‎; Job 28:12 תִּמָּצֵא מֵאַיַן וְהַחָכְמָה‎. (d) מִלֵּב‎ Isa 59:13; Job 8:10, especially with reference to what is self-devised, Num 16:28 מִלִּבִּי לֹא כִּי‎, 24:13; 1Kin 12:33; Neh 6:8; מִלִּבָּם נְבִיאֵי‎ Ezek 13:2.

d. of the source or author of an action, counsel, or event: 1Sam 24:14 רֶשַׁע יֵצֵא מֵרְשָׁעִים‎, 2Sam 3:37 לא מהמלך היתה‎ it was not from the king to, etc.; specifically of ׳י‎, Gen 24:50 מי ׳כי הדבר יצא‎, Judg 14:4 knew מי ׳כי הוא‎ that it was from J., 1Kin 2:15 מי כי לו ׳היתה‎, Prov 16:1; 20:24 ׳מי גֶבֶר מִצְעֲדֵי‎, Psa 37:39; 62:2 יְשׁוּעָתִי מִמֶּנּוּ‎, Hosea 8:4 they have made kings, וְלֹא מִמֶּנִּי‎ not from me, i.e. not at my prompting, Isa 30:1; 50:11 (מִיָּדִי‎) Ezek 3:17 end = 33:7 and warn them from me, 1Chr 5:22; 13:2; 2Chr 22:7; 25:20 (synonym מֵעִם מֵאֵת,‎, which are more frequent in this sense); in poetry Hosea 7:5 מִיַּיִן חֲמַת‎ heat from wine, Psa 9:14 עָנְיִי מִשּׂנְאַי‎ at the hands of my haters, 74:22; Job 4:13 לַיְלָה מֵחֶזְיֹנוֺת שְׂעִמִּים‎ thoughts (arising) out of, etc., 6:25 מִכֶּם הוֺכֵחַ‎ reproof proceeding from you, 20:29 (twice in verse), Psa 78:2 מִקֶּדֶם חִידוֺת‎ indirect lessons (springing) out of antiquity; Dan 11:31 מִמֶּנּוּ זְרֹעִים‎ (Köiii. 241). As marking the author of a judgment or estimate (rare), Num 32:22 מי ׳נְקִיִּם וּמִיִּשְׂרָאֵל‎ guiltless at the hands of (= in the judgment of) J. and Israel (compare מֵעִם‎ 2Sam 3:28; Job 34:33), 4:17 shall man be just מֵאֱלֹהַּ‎ at God's hands ? (|| מֵעשֵֹׁהוּ‎), Jer 51:5b (Ges Gf.); so in מי לִי ׳חָלִילָה‎.

e. of the immediate, or efficient, cause (chiefly in poetry), in consequence of, at by (compare Greek ἀπό, as Hd. 2:54 ζήησιν ἀπὸ σφέων γενέσθαι): (a) the cause, a person Gen 19:36 + מן הָֽרְתָה‎ to be pregnant by, 49:25; 1Sam 31:3 מֵהַמּוֺרִים וַיָּחֶל‎ was in anguish from the archers, Hosea 7:4 מֵאֹפֶה בֹּעֵ֫רָה‎ (ni הֵם בֹּעֵר‎ leg.: see We), Psa 18:9; Nahum 1:5 ממנו רעשׁו הרים‎, Dan 11:31 (accents); with passive verb, Nahum 1:6 ממנו נִתְּצוּ הצורים‎, Psa 37:23 (compare Prov 20:24

d), Job 24:1; Eccl 12:11; Dan 8:11. (b) the cause, a thing, Gen 49:24 his arms were agile יעקב אביר מידי‎ from the hands, etc., Isa 6:4 the thresholds shook הַקּוֺרֵא מִקּוֺל‎ (so מקול‎ elsewhere, as 30:31; 33:3; Jer 8:16), 28:7 מִןהַֿשֵּׁכָר תָעוּ‎ (|| ב‎), 31:4, 9; 10:10; Ezek 19:10 became fruitful רַבִּים מִמַּיִם‎, 31:5; Job 4:9 יאֹבֵדוּ אֱלוֺהַּ מִנִּשְׁמַת‎ at the breath of God, 14:9 יַפְרִחַ מַיִם מֵרֵיחַ‎, 31:23; 39:26 יַאֲבֶרנֵֿץ הֲמִבִּינָָֽתְךָ‎ Psa 39:11; 73:19 מִןבַּֿלָּהוֺת תַּמּוּ סָפוּ‎, 78:65 מִיַּיִן מִתְרוֺנֵן‎, 104:15 משׁמן פנים להצהיל‎ from oil, 107:39, compare Job 7:14 (|| ב‎); so with י ׳מִגַּעֲרַת‎ at J.'s rebuke, 18:16; Job 76:7 +; with a passive verb, Gen 9:11 to be cut off הַמַּבּוּל מִמֵּי‎, 2Sam 7:29 יְבֹרַח וּמִכִּכָֽתְךָ‎, Isa 28:7 מןהֿיין נבלעו‎ are undone through wine (22:3 is dubious: see 1b), Obadiah 9; Job 28:4 רָ֑גֶל מִנִּי הַנִּשְׁכָּחִים‎; compare Isa 34:3; Hosea 6:8. (c) with verbs of fearing, to express the source of the emotion, as ירא‎ Psa 3:7 + often (also with מִמְּנֵי‎), מָּחַד‎ 27:1, נִבְהַל‎ Ezek 26:18, גּוּר‎ Deut 18:22; Job 41:17; Est 5:9 ממנו זָע ולא ולאקֿם‎; with בּוֺשׁ‎ to be disconcerted or disappointed, to express the source of the disappointment, Isa 1:29 + often; with שָׂמֵחַ‎ Prov 5:18; Eccl 2:10. feminine of the remoter cause, the ultimate ground on account of which something happens or is done. (N.B. The line between

e and

f. is not always clearly defined): Exod 2:23 they sighed מןהֿעבדה‎ on account of the bondage, 6:9; 15:23; Deut 7:7 not מֵרֻבְּכֶם‎ through, by reason of, your numbers did J. set his love upon you, Josh 22:24 to do a thing מִדְּאָנָה‎ out of carefulness, 2Sam 23:4 מִנֹּגַהּ‎, 1Kin 14:4; Isa 53:5 wounded מִמְּשָׁעֵינוּ‎ on account of our transgressions, bruised מֵעֲוֺנוֺתֵינוּ‎, 53:8; Job 4:19; Obadiah 10; Hab 2:17; Psa 6:8 מִכַּעַס עיני עשׁשׁה‎ from vexation (compare Job 17:7: Psa 31:10 ׳ב‎), 31:12; 38:19 I am concerned on account of my sin, Prov 20:4 יחרשׁ לא עצל מֵחֹרֶף‎ by reason of the winter, Job 22:4 יֹכִיחֶ֑ךָ הֲמִיִּרְאָ֑תְךָ‎ on account of thy fear of him? Song 3:8; Ruth 1:13 מִכֶּם מְאֹד כִּימַֿרלִֿי‎ because of you: see also Deut 28:34, 67; 32:19; Judg 2:18; Isa 65:14; Jer 12:4; 24:2 מֵרֹעַ‎, 50:13; 51:5 b (Ew Ke), Ezek 7:27 (but read probably with ᵑ9 ᵑ6 ᵐ5‎ Co כְּדרכם‎), 16:61; 35:11 (AV out of), 45:20; Micah 2:12; 7:13; Psa 5:11; 12:6; 107:17; 119:53; Gen 49:12 red of eyes מִיָּ֑יִן‎, and white of teeth מֵחָלָב‎. Often also in מֵרֹב‎ from the abundance of, absolute for abundance, with many different verbs, as 16:10 מֵרֹב יִסָּפֵר לֹא‎ Josh 9:13; 1Sam 1:16, etc. Similarly in מִבִּלְתִּי מִבְּלִי, מֵאֵין,‎ (pp. 35, 115, 117); and before an infinitive (7a), and in מֵאֲשֶׁר‎ (p. 84).

g. the cause being conceived as regulative, מן‎ occasionally approaches in sense to according to (compare Latin ex more, ex lege), Jonah 3:7 proclaimed in Nineveh וגדליו המלך מטעם‎ at, by, in accordance with, the decree of the king (compare Aramaic Ezra 6:14; Dan 2:8): so Job 39:26 (2e (b)) according to Ges Hi.

3 Partitively (a sense connecting with

2a (c), above): —

a. Gen 6:19 מִכֹּל שְׁנַיִם‎ two out of, from, all, 7:8; 39:11 ֗֗֗ מן אישׁ‎ a man (or one) of . . . (so Num 25:6; 1 Samuel 24:28 +, ֗֗֗ מן אנשׁים‎ 16:2; Josh 2:2 +, 2Kin 2:7, etc.); Gen 42:16 send אֶחָד מִכֶּם‎ Lev 1:2a 17:12 מִכֶּם כלנֿפשׁ‎, 19:34; 26:8, Judg 8:14 סֻכּוֺת מֵאַנְשֵׁי נַעַר‎, 1Sam 22:8, etc.; Judg 14:19; 2Kin 2:24; Isa 66:19; ֗֗֗ מִן אֶחָד‎ 1Sam 16:18 +, ֗֗֗ מִן אַחַד‎ (Ges§ 130, 1) Deut 25:5 +; מֵהֵ֫נָּה אַחַת‎ Psa 34:21; Isa 34:16; ֗֗֗ מִן מִי‎ Job 5:1; Isa 50:1, ֗֗֗ מִן אֵין‎ 1Sam 14:39; Isa 51:18; 21:11 מלילה מהֿ‎ how much of the night? 2Chr 31:3 מִןרְֿכוּשׁוֺ הַמֶּלָח וּמְנָת‎.

b. the number being omitted, מִן‎ is used indefinitely: — (a) = some of, — as subject Exod 16:27 מןהֿעם יצאו‎ there went out (some) of the people, Lev 25:49; 2Sam 11:17, 24, especially in late Hebrew Ezra 2:68, 70; 7:7; Neh 11:4, 25; 1Chr 4:42; 9:30, 32; 2Chr 17:11; 32:21; Dan 11:35; more frequently as object, especially with לקח‎, Gen 4:3 האדמה מִמְּרִי וַיָּבֵא‎ brought of the fruit of the ground, 30:14 give me בְנֵךְ מִדּוּדָאֵי‎ (some) of thy son's love-apples, 33:15; Exod 12:7; 17:5; Lev 18:30; 20:2; Num 11:17; 13:23; 1Kin 12:4; Isa 39:7; 47:13; Amos 2:11; Dan 8:10 +, Song 1:2 מִּיו מִנְּשִׁיקוֺת ישׁקני‎ let him kiss me (with) some of the kisses etc., Psa 72:15; 137:3 צִיּוֺן מִשִּׁיר‎ (some) of the songs of Zion, Job 11:6 (Ges RVm) + often; in late Hebrew note also ֗֗֗ מִן יֵשׁ‎ there are some of . . . Neh 5:5; ֗֗֗ מֵהֶם ֗֗֗ מֵהֶם‎ some. . . others. . . 1Chr 9:28f. (as in Aramaic Dan 2:33, and PS2155); ֗֗֗ מִקְצָת‎ some of. . . (as in Late Hebrew) 1:2; Neh 7:69. (b) to designate an individual (rare), Gen 28:11 and he took הַמָּקוֺם מֵאַבְנֵי‎ (one) of the stones of the place (see 28:18), Exod 6:25 פוטיאל מבּנות‎ (one) of the daughters of P., Ezek 17:5, 13; Neh 13:28; Psa 132:11; as subject Lev 25:33; Dan 11:5 the king of the south וּמִןֿ שָׂרָיו‎ and (one) of his captains, 11:7, compare Jer 41:1; Est 4:5; 2Chr 26:11; Ruth 2:20 הוא מִגֹּאֲלֵנוּ‎ he is (one) of our kinsmen, Exod 2:6. (c) in a negative or hypothetical sentence (whether subject or object) = any, aught, Deut 16:4 מןהֿבשׂר ילין ולא‎ and there shall not remain any of the flesh, 1Kin 18:5 מןהֿבהמה נכרית ולא‎ and we shall not destroy any of the beasts, 2Kin 10:10 (compare Josh 21:43; 23:14; 1Sam 3:19; 1Kin 8:56; Est 6:10), Esther 6:23 י מֵעַבְדֵי ׳מֶּןיֶֿשׁמֹּֿה‎ Job 27:6 מִיָּמָ֑י לְבָבִי יֶחֱרַף לֹא‎ my heart reproacheth not one of my days: with אִם‎, etc. Exod 29:34; Lev 4:2a (compare 4:22; 4:27), 11:32 (מהם‎), 11:33; 11:35; 11:37-39; 18:29; 25:25; Num 5:6; מִכֹּל‎ anything whatever, Leviticus 5:24; Lev 11:34; compare 1Sam 23:23 (?). (d) peculiarly, with a noun of unity, especially אֶחָד‎, to express forcibly the idea of a single one: Deut 15:7 if there be a poor man in thy midst, אַחֶיךָ מֵאַחַר‎ any one of thy brethren, Lev 4:2b if he doeth מֵהֵ֫נָּה מֵאַחַת‎ any one of these things, 5:13; Ezek 18:10 אָח וְעָשָׂה מֵאֵלֶּה מֵאַחַד‎ (where אח‎ is a vox nihili) and doeth aught of these things; 1Sam 14:45 if there shall fall אַרְצָה ראֹשׁוֺ מִשַּׂעֲרַת‎ a single hair of his head to the ground! (for שְׂעָרָה‎ as a noun of individual meaning see Ges§ 122t Dr), compare 2Sam 14:11; 1Kin 1:52. (Probably a rhetorical application of the partitive sense, though the explanation 'starting from one' = 'even one' would also be possible. is used similarly after negative and interrogative particles, not merely with collective nouns, as nought have they of knowledge (Qor 18:4), but also with nouns of unity, as Qor 3:55 Ye have not aught of (= any) god, except Him; 19:19 dost thou perceive even one of them? 6:59 there falleth not even a single leaf (noun of individual meaning) without His knowing it. See further Thes, and WAG. ii. § 48 f. b), (e) (rare) specifying the objects, or elements, of which a Genus consists (the Arabic , min of explication, WAG. ii. § 48 g): Gen 6:2 מכל בחרו אשׁר‎ consisting of all whom they chose, 7:22; 9:10; Lev 11:32 (מכל‎), 1Chr 5:18; Jer 40:7 (מאשׁר‎); 44:28 and they shall know וּמֵהֶם מִמֶּנִּי יָקוּם דְּבַרמִֿי‎ whose word shall stand, consisting of me and of them (defining the Genus embraced by ׃מי‎ compare both (of them), Abel as well as Cain, and Qor 3:193: Wl.c.). — On מֵאַיִן‎ 10:6-7, see אַיִן‎ near the end.

4 of time — namely

a. as marking the terminus a quo, the anterior limit of a continuous period, from, since Deut 9:24 אֶתְכֶם דַּעְתִּי מִיּוֺם‎ from the day of my (first) knowing you (so 1Sam 7:2; 8:8 + ); 18:9 וָהָֽלְאָה ההוא מהיום‎ from that day and onwards, simil. Lev 22:27; Num 15:23; Ezek 39:22; Isa 18:2, 7 (where מִןהֿוּא‎ = הוּא מֵאֲשֶׁר‎; compare Nahum 2:9 הִיא מִימֵי‎ = הִיא אֲשֶׁר מִימֵי‎); וָמָֽעְלָה ההוא מהיום‎ 1Sam 16:13; 30:25 (Hag 2:15, 18 apparently of time backwards); מֵאָז‎ from the time of . . . .; מִןהַֿבֶּטֶן‎ from the womb Judg 13:5, 7, אִמִּי מִבֶּטֶן‎ 16:17 +; ֗֗֗ מִימֵי‎ Hosea 10:9; Isa 23:7; Jer 36:2 +; מִיָּמֶיךָ‎ idiomatic = since thou wast born 1Sam 25:28; 1Kin 1:6 (מִיָּמָיו‎), Job 38:12; מִקֶּדֶם‎ from antiquity Hab 1:12; Psa 74:12; Isa 42:14 מֵעוֺלָם הֶחֱשֵׁיתִי‎ I have been silent since old time; מֵעַתָּה‎ from now, hence-forth Jer 3:4 +, מִיּוֺם‎ from to-day 43:13; Ezek 48:35, הזה מןהֿיום‎ Hag 2:19. See also 5c, 7 c. compare Exod 33:6 חוֺרֵב מֵהַר‎ from Horeb, Hosea 13:4 I am ׳י‎ thy God מִצְרַיִם מֵאֶרֶץ‎.

b. as marking the period immediately succeeding the limit, after: Gen 38:24 חֳדָשִׁים כְּמִשְׁלשׁ‎ after about three months it was told Judah, רַבִּים מִיָּמִים‎ Josh 23:1; Ezek 38:8, מִיָּמִים‎ after (some) days, Judg 11:4; 14:8; 15:1, מִיֹּמַיִם‎ after two days Hosea 6:2; יָמִים מֵרֹב‎ Isa 24:22: more frequently with קֵץ‎ or קָצֶה‎, Gen 4:3 יָמִים מִקֵּץ‎, 8:3; Josh 3:2 + often; Deut 14:28 שָׁנִים שָׁלשׁ מִקְצֵה‎, 15:1 שֶׁבַע מִקְצֵה שָׁנִים‎ (by which is meant not the actual end of the three or seven years, but the period when the third or seventh year has arrived); מִמָּחֳרָת‎ after the morrow (had arrived) = on the morrow, Gen 19:34 + often; מֵהַבֹּקֶר‎ 2Sam 2:27. — 23:4 מִמָּטָר‎; Isa 53:11 נַפְשׁוֺ מֵעֲמַל‎; perhaps 29:18 (Kö581). compare 2Sam 20:5 and he delayed מןהֿמועד‎ beyond the appointed time.

c. in such phrases, however, מִן‎ sometimes (compare 1c) loses its significance: thus מֵאָז‎ 2Sam 15:34; Isa 16:13 not from former time, but in former time, formerly, Gen 6:4 מֵעוֺלָם אֲשֶׁר הַגִּבּוֺרִים‎ which were of old, Josh 24:2 dwelt of old, Psa 77:6 days מִקֶּדֶם‎ aforetime, מֵאַחֲרֵי‎ Deut 29:21 (p. 30). — מִקָּרוֺב‎ literally from near, i.e. recently 32:17, of short duration Job 20:5, shortly Ezek 7:8; at hand (in a local sense, 1c) Jer 23:23.

5 (וְעַד‎) עַד ֗֗֗ מִן‎ from . . . even, to : very oft .: —

a. in geography or local sense, Gen 10:19; 15:18 הגדול הנהר עד מצרים מנהר‎, 25:18; Exod 23:31; Deut 2:36; 1Sam 3:20; 2Sam 5:25; Jer 31:38; Psa 72:8 + often; so with מִלְּבוֺא‎ 1Kin 8:65 (2Chr 7:8), 2Kin 14:25; Amos 6:14; Deut 13:8 הָאָרֶץ קְצֵה וְעַד הָאָרֶץ מִקְצֵה‎, 28:64; Jer 12:12; Gen 47:21 וְעַדקָֿצֵהוּ גְּבוּלמִֿצְרַיִם מִקְצֵה‎, 1Kin 6:24; 7:23 וְעַד מִשְּׂפָתוֺ שְׂפָתוֺ‎; Lev 13:12 רגליו ועד מראשׁו‎, Deut 28:35 רגלך מכף קדקדך ועד‎ (similarly 2Sam 14:25; Job 2:7; Isa 1:6). compare 1Sam 9:2 וָמַ֫עְלָה מִשִּׁכְמוֺ‎, 2Sam 5:9; Josh 15:46.

b. metaphor not of actual space, but of classes of objects, to express idiomatically the idea ofcomprehension, so that the two prepositions may be often represented by both . . . and: Gen 19:4 וְעַדזָֿקֵן מִנַּעַר‎ from young to old (i.e. both included) = both young and old, 19:11; 1Sam 5:9 + וְעַדגָּֿדוֺל מִקָּטֹן‎ = both great and small, Jer 6:13 וְעַדגְּֿדוֺלָם מִקְּטַנָּם‎ from the least of them even to the greatest of them, ib. מִנָּבִיא וְעַדכֹּֿהֵן‎ from the prophet even to the priest every one dealeth falsely, Exod 9:25 + בהמה ועד מאדם‎ both man and beast, 11:5 וגו השׁפחה ׳בכור פרעהע֗֗֗ד מבכור‎, 13:15; Num 6:4; Deut 29:10 עציך מחֹטב מימיך שֹׁאב עד‎, Josh 8:25 + אשׁה ועד מאישׁ‎, 1Sam 15:3 (4 pairs), 22:19; 1Kin 5:13; 2Kin 17:9 = 18:8, Isa 10:18 בשׂר ועד מנפשׁ‎ = both soul and body, Jer 9:9; after a word implying a negative = either . . . or Gen 14:23; 31:24, 29 רע עד מטוב‎ either good or evil. The עַד‎ may be repeated, if required: 6:7 מאדם השׁמים ועדעֿוף רמשׂ עד עדבֿהמה‎ (so 7:23), Exod 22:3; Josh 6:21; Judg 15:5 זָ֑יִת וְעַדכֶּֿרֶם וְעַדקָֿמָה מִגָּדִישׁ‎, 20:48; 1Sam 30:19: without מן‎, Lev 11:42; Num 8:4. Similar is the use of מן‎ in the idiom (וָמָֽטָּה‎) וָמָֽעְלָה מִבֶּןשָׁ֗֗֗נָה‎ (also שָׁנָה ֗֗֗ וְעַדבֶּֿן‎); and compare 2Kin 3:21

c. of time, Gen 46:34 עַתָּה וְעַד מִנְּעֻרֵינוּ‎ from our youth even until now, 1Sam 12:2; Jer 3:25; Num 14:19; Exod 10:6; 18:13 עדהֿערב מןהֿבֹקר‎, 1Sam 30:17; 1Kin 18:26; Isa 9:6; Psa 90:2; + often: with two inff. Hosea 7:4: and implying intervals (not duration) Ezek 4:10-11, (compare with לְ‎ Est 3:7 (twice in verse)).

d. there occur further (1) אֶלֿ ֗֗֗ מִן‎, Josh 15:21; Exod 26:28 = 36:33 אֶלהַֿקָּצֶה מִןהַֿקָּצֶה‎ from end to end, Ezek 40:23, 27; Ezra 9:11 מִמֶּהאֶֿלמֶּֿה‎; Psa 144:13 זַן אֶל מִזַּן‎ from kind to kind = kinds of every sort; with a verb of motion, Jer 48:11; Psa 105:13; 1Chr 17:5, and expressing a climax, Psa 84:8 אֶלחַֿיִל מֵחַיִל יֵָֽלְכוּ‎, Jer 9:2 (compare Rom 1:17): of time, מיוםאֿליֿום‎ Num 30:15, compare 1Chr 16:23 (|| Psa 96:2 לְ‎); implying intervals, אֶלעֵֿת מֵעֵת‎ 1Chr 9:25. (2) לְ ֗֗֗ מִן‎ Exod 32:27; Ezek 40:13; Zech 14:10: of time Psa 96:2; Job 4:20: with intervals, 2Sam 14:26. (3) הָ֯ ֗֗֗ מִן‎ Num 34:10; Ezek 6:14; רִבְלָ֫תָה מִמִּדְבָּר‎ (so Ges Ew Hi etc.) from the wilderness to Riblah, 21:3; 25:13 וּדְדָ֫נֶה מִתֵּימָן‎ (Co Kö Berthol); without ָ֯‎ 1Kin 5:1. And of time in the phrase (implying intervals) יָמִ֫ימָה מִיָּמִים‎ Exod 13:10 4t.

6 In comparisons, beyond, above, hence in English than: so constantly: namely

a. when an object is compared with another distinct from itself, Judg 14:18 מִדְּבַשׁ מַהמָּֿתוֺק‎ what is sweet away from, beyond in excess of, honey ? i.e. in our idiom, what is sweeter than honey ? Lev 21:10 מֵאֶחָיו הַגָּדוֺל הַכֹּהֵן‎ the priest that is great above his brethren, Num 14:12; Ezek 28:3 מִדָּנִאֵל חָכָם‎ wiser than Daniel, Psa 119:72 + very often; Hosea 2:9 מֵעָ֑תָּה אָז לִי טוֺב כִּי‎; with an infinitive (sometimes with לְ‎) as subject, Gen 29:10 וגו אֹתָהּ מִתִּתִּי לְךָ אֹתָהּ תִּתִּי ׳טוֺב‎ better is my giving her to thee than my giving her to another, Exod 14:12; 1Sam 15:22; Prov 21:9, 19; 25:7; Psa 118:8; 118:9 +; with verbs, Gen 19:9 מֵהֶם לְךָ נָרַע עתה‎ now we will harm thee beyond them, more than them, 25:23 יֶאֱמַץ מִלְאֹם לְאֹם‎, 26:16; 29:30 גםֿ ויאהב מִלֵּאָה אתרֿחל‎, 38:26 מִמֶּנִּי צָֽדְקָה‎, 48:19 מִמֶּנּוּ יִגְדַּל‎, Judg 2:19 מאבותם השׁחיתו‎ they have done corruptly more than their fathers, 1Sam 2:29; 2Sam 20:6; 1Kin 1:37; 14:9; Jer 5:3; Ezek 5:6 + often; = in, preference to, above, Psa 45:8; 52:5 (twice in verse); Hosea 6:6; Hab 2:16, after בחר‎ Jer 8:3; Job 7:15; 36:21; Psa 84:11 (מִדּוּר‎) +: note also מִן נֹפֵל‎ Job 12:3; 13:2 +?to (Ew Ges and others Hi; al. De); מִן שֹׁנֶה‎ different from Est 1:7; 3:8.

b. when an object is compared with a group or multitude of which it forms one, especially with מִכֹּל‎, Gen 3:1 עָרוּם הַשָּׂדֶה חַיַּת מִכֹּל‎ subtil out of all beasts of the field, or beyond, above all (other) beasts, 3:14 cursed above all cattle (but without implying any judgment whether other cattle are cursed likewise), 37:3 Israel loved Joseph מִכָּלבָּֿנָיו‎ out of all his sons, or above all his (other) sons, Deut 7:7; 33:24 אָשֵׁר מִבָּנִים בָּרוּךְ‎ blessed above sons be Asher, Judg 5:24 מִנָּשִׁים תְּבֹרַח‎ blessed above women be Jael, 1Sam 9:2b 15:33 אִמֶּ֑ךָ מִנָּשִׁים תִּשְׁכַּל כֵּן‎, 18:30; Jer 17:9 מִכֹּל עָקֹב‎ deceitful above all things, Psa 45:3; Song 5:10 מֵרְבָבָה דָּגוּל‎ (compare מִן בָּחַר‎ above

2a c: ex in eximius, egregius; Iliad 18:431 ὅς σ’, ἐμοὶ ἐκ πάσεων Κρονίδης Ζεὺς ἄλγἐ ἔδωκεν, 3:227 ἔξοχος Ἀργείων . . . κεφαλήν).

c. sometimes in poetry the idea on which מן‎ is logically dependent, is unexpressed, and must be understood by the reader, Isa 10:10 מירושׁלם ופסיליהם‎ and their idols are (more) than (those of) Jerusalem, Micah 7:4 מִמְּסוּכָה יָשָׁר‎ the uprightest is (sharper) than a thorn-hedge (but We from), Job 11:7; 28:18; Psa 4:8 מֵעֵת‎ beyond (that of) the time when etc. Ecclesiastes 4:17; Eccl 9:17; compare Ezek 15:2.

d. מן‎ not unfrequently expresses the idea of a thing being too much for a person, or surpassing his powers: Gen 18:14 ׳מי הֲיִמָּלֵא דָּבָר‎ can a thing be too hard for J.? (so Deut 17:8 +; compare Psa 131:1; 139:6 + ), 32:11 מִן קָטֹנְתִּי‎, Deut 14:24 הַדֶּרֶךְ מִמְּךָ יִרְבֶּה כִּי‎ = is too great for thee (1Kin 19:7), 1Ki 32:47 מִכֶּם רֵק‎: so with עָצַם‎ Gen 26:16, כָּבֵד‎ be too heavy for Exod 18:18; Psa 38:5, מָךְ‎ Lev 27:8 (too poor to pay), קָשָׁה‎ Deut 1:7, צַר‎ be too narrow for, 2Kin 6:1; Isa 49:19, קצר‎ 50:2, אָמַץ‎ Psa 18:18, נמני ירום‎ is too high for me 61:3, גָּבַר‎ 65:4; מִמְּךָ ַהמְעַט‎ Job 15:11 too little for thee ? מִכֶּם ַהמְעַט‎ Num 16:9; Isa 7:13; Ezek 34:18 (see מְעַט‎; also on 16:20); often with an infinitive, as Gen 4:13 מִנְּשׂוֺא עֲוֺנִי גָּדוֺל‎ is greater than I can bear, 30:7 their substance was יַחְדָּו מִשֶּׁבֶת רַב‎ literally great beyond dwelling together = too great for (their) dwelling together, Exod 12:4; Judg 7:2 רַב מִתִּתִּי‎ = too great for me to give, 1Sam 25:17b 1Kin 8:64 מֵהָכִיל רַב‎, Isa 28:20; 33:19; 59:1; Hab 1:13; Psa 40:6; Ruth 1:12: note especially מִן רַב‎ it is more than that . . . (= there is enough of), Exod 9:28; 1Kin 12:28, followed by substantive Ezek 44:6 (see רַב‎); and Isa 49:6 וגו לְהָקִים ׳עֶבֶד לִי מִהְיוֺתְךָ נָקֵל‎ too light for thy being my servant was it to raise up, etc., Ezek 8:17 וגו ׳מֵעֲשׂוֺת יִשְׂר לְבֵית ׳הֲנָקֵל‎ was it too trifling to the house of Israel for the doing etc. (less than the doing etc. deserved) ? (but ? read עֲשׂוֺת‎ on analogue of 1Kin 16:31).

7 מן‎ is prefixed to an infin.:

a. with a causal force (rare), from, on account of, through (compare 2f): Deut 7:7-8, י ׳מֵאַהֲבַת אֶתְכֶם‎ through J.'s loving you = because J. loved you, 9:28 (compare 1:27 בְּ‎) 2Sam 3:11 אֹתוֺ מִיִּרְאָתוֺ‎ = because he feared him, Isa 48:4 ֗֗֗ מִדַּעְתִּי‎ = because I knew. . . So in מִבִּלְתִּי , ֗֗֗ מִבְּלִי‎.

b. after verbs implying restraint, prevention, cessation, etc., as עֲצָרַנִי מִלֶּדֶת‎ Gen 16:2 hath restrained me from bearing, מִלֶּדֶת וַתַּעֲמֹד‎ 29:35; 30:9: so with חשׂך‎ 20:6 +, חדל‎ + Exod 23:5 +, כִּלָּה‎ + 34:33 +, נִכְלָא‎ 36:6, מָנַע‎ 1Sam 25:26 +, שׁבת‎ Jer 31:36 +, מֵהַבִּיט יָרֵא‎ Exod 3:6 +, מִןהַֿחֵרֶם שִׁמְרוּ‎ Josh 6:18; 2Chr 25:13 מִלֶּכֶת הֵשִׁיב‎. Especially (a) after similar verbs, expressing concisely a negative consequence, literally away from . . ., i.e. so as not to, so that not: Gen 23:6; b 27:1 Jacob's eyes were dim, ֵמרְאֹת‎ away from seeing = so that he could not see, 31:29 מִן נִשְׁמַר‎ (|| 31:24 מֶּן‎), Exod 14:5; Lev 26:13; Num 32:7; Deut 28:55 (his eye shall be envious etc.) מִתֵּת‎ from giving = so that he will not give, Judg 6:27; 1 Samuel 21:31; 1Sam 7:8 do not be silent from us מִזְּעֹק‎ so as not to call (compare 1Kin 22:3), 1Sam 8:7 me have they rejected עליהם מִמְּלֹךְ‎, 16:1 (Hosea 4:6), 2Sam 14:11 (read מֵהַרְבּוֺת‎), Isa 5:6; 8:11; 21:3; 23:1 is destroyed מִבּוֺא‎ so that none can enter in, 24:10; 33:15; 44:18; 49:15; 54:9; 56:6; 58:13; Jer 10:14 מִדַּעַת ֗֗֗ נִבְעַר‎ is stupefied so that he has no knowledge, 13:14; 33:21, 24, 26; Ezek 20:17; Micah 3:6; Zech 7:11; 7:12; Psa 30:4 Qr, 39:2; 69:24; 102:5 (after שָׁכַח‎, peculiarly), 106:23; Lam 3:44; 4:18; Job 34:30a 2Chr 36:13. So in מֵעֲשׂוֺת חָלִילָהלִֿי‎ that I should not do Gen 44:17 +. (b) still more concisely, especially in poetry, with a noun alone: 1Sam 15:23 has rejected thee מִמֶּלֶךְ‎ from (being) king (15:26 מִהְיוֺת מֶלֶךְ‎), Lev 26:43 מֵהֶם‎, Isa 7:8 מֵעָם יֵחַת‎ shall be shattered from (being) a people, that it be no more a people, 17:1 מֵעִיר מוּסָר‎, 25:2b; 52:14 מִשְׁחַת כֵּן מַרְאֵהוּ מֵאִישׁ‎ marred away from (being) a man('s), Jer 2:25 מִיָּחֵף‎, 17:16 מֵרֹעֶה‎, 48:2 מִגּוֺי וְנַכְרִיתֶנָּה‎, 48:42 מֵעָם‎, Psa 8:6 hast made him lack but little מאלהים‎ ut non esset Deus, 83:5 מִגּוֺי‎, Prov 30:2 בַּעַר מֵאִישׁ אָנֹכִי‎ too boorish to be a man: compare Dan 4:13; 1Kin 15:13 מִגְּבִירָה וַיְסִרֶהָ‎ removed her from (being) queen-mother, Ezek 16:41 מִזּוֺנָה וִהִשְׁבַּתִּיךְ‎; and even to express absolutely the non-existence of a thing not named in the principal clause, as Isa 23:1 כִּי מִבַּיִת שֻׁדַּד‎ so that there is no house, Ezek 12:19 (32:15), 25:9 מֵהֶעָרִים‎, Hosea 9:11 (3 t. in verse); 9:12; Micah 3:6; Hag 1:10 מִטָּ֑ל‎, Zech 7:14; 9:8; Psa 39:3; 49:15 מִזְּבֻללֿוֺ‎ so that it has no dwelling, 52:7 מֵאֹהֶל יִסָּֽחֲךָ‎ pluck thee up tentless, 109:24 is lean מִשָּׁ֑מֶן‎ so that there is no fatness, Job 28:11; 33:21; 34:30b. Oft. strengthened by pleonastic אֵין‎ or בְּלִי‎, as יוֺשֵׁב מֵאֵין‎ Isa 5:9, יוֺשֵׁב מִבְּלִי‎ see pp. 35:a, 115:b. compare Köiii. 592 ff.

c. with a temporal force, since, after (compare

4), chiefly late: Num 24:23 אֵל מִשֻּׂמוֺ‎ after God's establishing him, Isa 44:7 עֿוֺלָם עַם מִשֻּׂמִי‎ since I appointed the ancient people, Hosea 7:4; Hag 2:16 (?) Ruth 2:18; Neh 5:14; 1Chr 8:8 אוֺתָם מִןשִֿׁלְחוֺ‎ (compare 6:16) 2Chr 31:10; Dan 11:23; 12:1 (compare 9:25), Psa 73:20 מֵהָקִיץ כַּחֲלוֺם‎ after (one's) awaking, Job 20:4.

8 Once Deut 33:11 as a

conjunction before a finite verb. Smite . . . his haters מִןיְֿקוּמוּן‎ that they rise not again, in poetry for מִקּוּם‎ (7b): compare Dr§ 41. — On מֵאֲשֵׁר‎

adverb and

conjunction.

9 In compounds: —

a. מִלְּ מִבַּ֫עַד, מִבַּלְעֲדֵי, מִבֵּין, מֵאֵת, מֵאַחֲרֵי,‎ (common in Late Hebrew, **for מִלְּ‎ in Mishna see e.g. Babylonian Mez 7:10; Kil 8:1; Ter 8:11; Pes 1:6; Taan 2:7; Yeb 8:2; Ecclesiastes 4:17 מִלַּעֲשׂוֺת‎ (have no knowledge so as not to do evil) is read by Siegf Wild; especially before infinitive; in O.T. only in מִלְּבוֺא מִלְּבַד,‎ (above 5a), מִלִּפְנֵי מִלְּפָנִים, מִלְּעֻמַּת, מִלְמַ֫טָּה, מִלְמַ֫עְלָה,‎, and, si vera lectio, הֶחָ֑רֶס מִלְמַעֲלֵה‎ Judg 8:13, see מַעֲלֶה‎), מִתַּ֫חַת מֵעִם, מֵעַל, מִנֶּגֶד,‎; see אֵת אַחֲרֵי,‎, etc.

b. לְמִן‎ (לְמִנִּי‎ Micah 7:12 (twice in verse)), with לְ‎ pleonastic, from = מִן‎, but used almost exclusively of the terminus a quo, whether of space or time (compare מִן‎

5); — (I) of space, Deut 4:32; Judg 20:1 שֶׁבַע וְעַדבְּֿאֵר לְמִדַּן‎, Micah 7:12.7:12 (both לְמִנִּי‎), Zech 14:10; 1Chr 5:9; לְמֵרָחוֺק‎ from afar Job 36:3; 39:29 (on Ezra 3:13; 2Chr 26:15, see below לְ עַד‎); לְ לְמִתַּחַת‎ = underneath 1Kin 7:32. Idiomatic, especially followed by וְעַד‎, to denote comprehensively an entire class, בְּהֵמָה וְעַד לְמֵאִישׁ‎ Exod 11:7; Jer 51:62 (לְמֵאָדָם‎), אִשָּׁה וְעַד לְמֵאִישׁ‎ 2Sam 6:19; 2Chr 15:13, גָּדוֺל וְעַד לְמִקָּטֹן‎ 2Kin 23:2; Jer 42:8, simil. 2Chr 15:13; Jer 31:34; Est 1:5, 20, וְעַדטֿוֺב לְמֵרָע‎ 2Sam 13:22, שָׁנָה עֶשְׂרִים לְמִבֶּן וּלְמָ֑טָּה‎ 1Chr 27:23, compare 2Chr 25:5. — On לְמִבֵּית‎ Num 18:7. (2) of time (often following by עַד‎), ֗֗֗ אֲשֶׁר הַיּוֺם לְמִן‎ from the day when . . ., Deut 4:32; 9:7; 2Sam 7:11 (|| 1Chr 17:10 אֲשֶׁר וּלְמִיָּמִים‎) Jer 7:25; 32:31; Hag 2:18; ֗֗֗ אֲשֶׁר הַיָּמִים לְמִקְצָת‎ Dan 1:18; הַיּוֺם לְמִן‎ followed by infinitive (in apposition) Exod 9:18; 2Sam 19:25; לְמִיּוֺם‎ followed by infinitive (genitive) Judg 19:30; 2Sam 7:6; Isa 7:17; ֗֗֗ לְמִימֵי‎ 2Kin 19:25 (|| Isa 37:26 מימי‎) Mal 3:7; למןֿ עולם ועד עולם‎ Jer 7:7; 25:5; לְמֵרָחוֺק‎ from afar = long before, 2Sam 7:19 = 1Chr 17:17; 2Kin 19:25 = Isa 37:26.

מְנָאוֺת‎ see מְנָת‎ below מנה‎. below

[מַנְגִּינָה‎] see נגן‎.

II. מִנֵּי מִנִּי,‎ see מִן‎. מִנִּי‎ Psa 45:9 see I. [ מֵן‎].
